They aren't orphans. All three exist solely to serve a commented-out JSX block at lines 359–380 — the base SFCC Account and Wishlist **icon buttons**:

```jsx
{/* <IconButtonWithRegistration
      icon={<AccountIcon />}
      aria-label={… 'My Account' …}
      onClick={onMyAccountClick}
    />
    <IconButtonWithRegistration
      icon={<HeartIcon />}
      aria-label={… 'Wishlist' …}
      onClick={onWishlistClick}
    /> */}
```

## What's actually wrong

**My first read was wrong on two counts.** I said they were "left behind by the `BrandLogo` → `ZimmLogo` swap" and that the fix was to delete the imports. Neither holds — they predate that swap, and deleting the imports while leaving the block would strand it.

Here's what the evidence actually says:

**1 · The block is *superseded*, not *pending*.** Line 230 of the same file:

```jsx
{/* Desktop right: Account | Saved | Bag as text */}
```

and at line 245:

```jsx
<ButtonWithRegistration onClick={onMyAccountClick}>
```

The Zimmermann header design replaced base SFCC's **icon** buttons with **text** buttons. `ButtonWithRegistration` supersedes `IconButtonWithRegistration`; text labels supersede `AccountIcon`/`HeartIcon`.

**2 · The requirement is satisfied.** `.docs/prd/homepage.md:18` — HPC-018, Confirmed:

> The confirmed header icon set is: **Search, Account, and Bag**.

Account is present — as text. So commenting out the icon version isn't a regression against a confirmed requirement. Same for Wishlist, which the header renders as "Saved".

**3 · It's been dead since day one.** `git log -L` traces the commenting to `cd60b7a Initial commit during Detailed Design phase` — i.e. it was disabled the moment the file was copied into `overrides/`. That's the **copy-first rule working as designed**: copy the base file verbatim, comment out what you're replacing. It was a deliberate reference marker, not an accident.

**4 · And the rule collision is real.** AGENTS.md:

> **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually.

So this is a decision for you, not a cleanup a reviewer performs.

## How to fix it — three options

**Option A · Leave it, document why** *(zero risk, 3 warnings remain)*
Add a line above the import block:
```tsx
// AccountIcon / HeartIcon / IconButtonWithRegistration support the commented-out base
// SFCC icon-button block below (~L359). Superseded by the Account | Saved | Bag text
// buttons per the Zimmermann header design; kept as a reference to the base implementation.
```

**Option B · Delete block and imports together** *(my recommendation)*
AGENTS.md explicitly permits removing commented code *"when removing the corresponding code"* — and here the block **is** the corresponding code. Removes ~25 lines and all 3 warnings.

Justified because: the block is superseded by a shipped alternative rather than awaiting a decision; it's been dead since the initial commit; git history preserves it if anyone ever wants it back; and the file gets a Tier 2 review regardless.

**Option C · `eslint-disable` with a reason**
Keeps the block, silences the warnings, states the reason at the point of use. Middle ground, but it adds a suppression to carry forever for code nobody intends to restore.

## What I'd do

**Option B.** The usual reason to preserve commented-out code is "we might need this back" — that doesn't apply when a working replacement is already shipping in the same file and the PRD confirms the replacement satisfies the requirement.

One caveat worth your judgement: `header/index.tsx` is **Tier 2 shared shell**, owned by both squads. Deleting 25 lines of base-template reference from it is the kind of thing the other squad might reasonably want to know about, even though it's inert.

Want me to make the Option B change? It's a small, contained edit — and I'd leave it uncommitted alongside the item 7 work for you to review.

text:
ngs in `theme/components/`.

**4 · It's the single biggest blocker on item 6.** 29 of the branch's `cssVars` references are in this one file. Nothing else comes close.

**5 · The mixed idiom is confusing.** Two elements already use `chakra.div sx={{}}` with a proper `_hover` and a WCAG-correct `_focusVisible` — so the component *half* knows the pattern. The other six elements are raw inline styles.

## The one thing that legitimately stays

`floated = value !== '' || focused` drives the label position and input opacity. CSS can express `:focus-within`, but "has a value" isn't reliably expressible without a `:placeholder-shown` trick that changes the markup contract.

**So `floated` stays in JS** — it just gets passed *into* the recipe rather than used to pick colours in the component.

## How to fix it

Convert to a Chakra **multipart recipe with a prop-driven `baseStyle`**. Chakra 2.7.0 supports this — `baseStyle` can be a function receiving props.

**`theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts`:**

```ts
export const ZimmTextInput = {
  parts: ['root', 'row', 'content', 'label', 'input', 'clearButton', 'helper', 'error'],
  baseStyle: ({ inverse, disabled, hasError, floated }) => ({
    root:  { display: 'block', width: '100%', opacity: disabled ? 0.4 : 1 },
    row:   {
      display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 'xs',
      borderBottom: '…',                       // the borderColour table moves here
      _hover: disabled ? undefined : { borderBottomColor: '…' },
    },
    label: { /* the floated ? … : … branches */ },
    input: { /* … */ },
    clearButton: { /* keeps the existing _focusVisible */ },
    helper: { /* inverse branch */ },
    error:  { /* inverse branch */ },
  }),
}
```

**In the component:**

```tsx
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', { inverse, disabled, hasError, floated })

<chakra.div __css={styles.root}>
  <chakra.div __css={styles.row}>
    <chakra.label __css={styles.label} htmlFor={inputId}>{label}</chakra.label>
    <chakra.input __css={styles.input} … />
```

**The hook slims to what it should own** — `value`, `focused`, `floated`, `inputRef`, `handleChange`, `handleClear`, `setFocused`. The three `*Colour` returns disappear.

`zimmInputAction` is trivial by comparison: one `<form style={{display:'block', width:'100%'}}>` → `<chakra.form>`. Its `useState` is `validationError` — real validation state, which stays.

## The trade-off worth knowing about

**7 of the 19 tests you just wrote cover colour derivation** (`inverse mode uses the inverse palette`, `hover keeps the error colour when in error`, `disabled uses the subtle colour for the mode`, etc.). If the colour table moves to the recipe, those tests no longer describe the hook.

**But they don't die — they get simpler.** A recipe `baseStyle` is a plain function, so testing it needs no `renderHook`:

```ts
expect(ZimmTextInput.baseStyle({ inverse: true, hasError: true }).row.borderBottom)
  .toContain('…')
```

That's a cheaper test than the hook version, and it tests the thing the designer actually edits. So the migration relocates the coverage rather than losing it — worth doing the test move in the same commit so nothing is uncovered in between.

## Why it's worth it

- Kills **29 of the branch's `cssVars` references** in one file — the single biggest step toward deleting `cssVars.ts` (item 6)
- Makes the last non-conformant atom themeable, so a designer token change actually reaches it
- Removes the orphaned-stub smell — the registered recipe finally does something
- Leaves `zimmButton`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` all on the same pattern, which is what a reviewer will look for

**Effort: this is the largest remaining item — roughly half a day**, most of it in getting the label/input `floated` branches right and moving the 7 tests. Everything else in the list is minutes to an hour.

Want me to do it? I'd suggest committing items 2/3/4/7/8 first so this lands as its own reviewable diff rather than merging into the pile.

## What changed

| File | Before → After |
|---|---|
| `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` | 8-line empty stub → **173-line multipart recipe** |
| `atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx` | 191 → **115 lines** |
| `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.ts` | 118 → **63 lines** |
| `molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx` | `<form style={{}}>` → `<chakra.form __css>` |
| `theme/components/zimmTextInput.test.ts` | **new**, 13 tests |
| `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.test.ts` | 19 → 10 tests (colour coverage relocated) |

## The mechanism table now

| Component | `useState` | inline style | recipe | `cssVars` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zimmButton` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `zimmIcon` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **`zimmTextInput`** | **0** *(was 1)* | **0** *(was 6)* | **10** *(was 0)* | **0** *(was 29)* |
| `zimmNavItem` | 0 | 0 | 4 | 2 |
| `zimmInputAction` | 1 *(validation)* | **0** *(was 1)* | 1 | 0 |
| `zimmLogo` | 0 | 1 | 0 | 2 |

**29 `cssVars` references eliminated from one file** — that was the branch's single largest consumer, and the main thing standing between you and deleting `cssVars.ts`.

## How it's structured

The recipe takes the state the theme can't observe and resolves the Figma cascade itself:

```ts
baseStyle: ({inverse, disabled, focused, filled}) => ({
  root, row, content, label, input, clearButton, helper, error
})
```

with three exported resolvers — `resolveBorderColour`, `resolveHoverBorderColour`, `resolveLabelColour` — carrying the precedence rules and their Figma comments.

The component feeds it back:

```tsx
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', {
  inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled: value.length > 0,
})
```

The hook now owns only what React must: value, focus, `floated`, the ref and the handlers. **Both the controlled/uncontrolled logic from item 2 and the WCAG 2.5.8 24px target and 2.4.7 focus ring survived intact** — the latter two now live in the `clearButton` part.

## On the test trade-off

I flagged that 9 colour tests would be invalidated. They weren't lost — they moved and got cheaper. No `renderHook`, just direct function calls:

```ts
expect(resolveBorderColour({...base, hasError: true, filled: true}))
  .toBe('var(--zimm-color-status-error)')
```

Plus 4 new wiring tests the hook version couldn't express — every declared part is produced, the row border reflects the resolved colour, `_hover` is suppressed when disabled, and the floated label switches size and position.

**Net: 160 → 164 tests.** All 5 files pass, `tsc` clean, **0 non-prettier lint problems** on everything I touched.

## Two things worth knowing

**I hit one type error and fixed it** — `_hover` isn't on `SystemStyleObject`'s plain-CSS surface, so that assertion needed a `Record<string, unknown>` cast with a comment explaining why.

**Prettier counts went up** (recipe 138, component 93) for the same reason as item 7 — I matched the files' aligned-colon house style, which prettier disagrees with. Item 1 normalises all of it in one pass; doing it now would bury this diff.

## Remaining after this

`zimmLogo` is the last holdout — 1 inline style and 2 `cssVars` refs, both for the SVG `fill` and the provisional `327px`/`39px` already flagged for Kiera. Small.

For **item 6**, the `cssVars.ts` importers are now: `footer/index.tsx` (35), `zimmNavItem` (2), `zimmLogo` (2), the hook's test — gone — and 5 story files. The heavy one left is the footer.

Working tree now has seven modified files and two untracked tests across items 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 — all green. Want me to run item 1 (`eslint --fix`) now to normalise the lot?

5 removed 29 of them, so what's left is one real job and seven small ones:

| Importer | Refs | What it uses |
|---|---|---|
| `components/footer/index.tsx` | **35** | `color.text` ×9, `spacing.*` ×15, `color.opacity[50]` ×2, 5 `cssTextStyles` |
| 5 story files | 15 | `color.background['05']`, `color.text`, `spacing.xl` |
| `atoms/zimmNavItem` | 1 | `font.family.body` |
| `atoms/zimmLogo` | 2 | `color.text.inverse` / `.default` for the SVG `fill` |

## What's wrong

**Being straight: it isn't broken.** I checked all 91 var names against `zimmTokens.ts` — **0 drifted.** So this is a maintenance-risk argument, not a live-defect one.

**1 · It's a second set of names for values that already have names.** Every entry maps to something already registered in the theme. `cssVars.color.text.default` and `color="text.default"` resolve to the same value; one is registered and type-checked, the other is a hand-typed string.

**2 · The sync is hand-maintained and nothing tests it.** `theme/index.test.tsx`'s 125 guards know nothing about this file. Rename a key in `zimmTokens.ts` and the failure is **silent** — an unresolved CSS custom property produces no error, just no style. Currently clean; nothing keeps it that way.

**3 · The type makes a typo compile.**

```ts
export const cssTextStyles: Record<string, Record<string, string>> = {
```

Any string key typechecks. `cssTextStyles.captionn` returns `undefined`, spreads nothing, and renders an unstyled element with no warning at build or runtime. That's a real latent hazard — I went looking for exactly this and only didn't find it because nobody's typo'd yet.

**4 · `button` and `buttonSm` duplicate what `button.ts` owns.** #56 deliberately removed `.zimm-text-btn-lg/-sm` from `globalStyles.ts` and made `button.ts` the single source for button styling. These two presets reintroduce that duplication one layer up.

## How to fix it

Nothing new needs writing — every value already has a registered equivalent:

| `cssVars` expression | Replacement | Registered as |
|---|---|---|
| `cssVars.color.text.default` | `color="text.default"` | `theme.colors` |
| `cssVars.color.background['05']` | `bg="background.05"` | `theme.colors` |
| `cssVars.spacing.xl` | `p="xl"` / `mb="xl"` | `theme.space` |
| `cssTextStyles.caption` | `textStyle="caption"` | `theme.textStyles` |
| `cssVars.font.family.body` | `fontFamily="body"` | `theme.fonts` |
| `cssVars.color.opacity[50]` | `var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)` in a recipe | — |

**Order of operations** — deliberate, because each step shrinks the next:

| Step | Files | Work |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 stories | `cssVars.color.background['05']` → `bg="background.05"`. They render inside `ChakraProvider`, so this just works |
| 2 | `zimmLogo` | 2 refs → `currentColor` or a `useToken` lookup for the SVG `fill` |
| 3 | `zimmNavItem` | 1 ref → move `fontFamily` into `zimmNavItem.ts` |
| 4 | **`footer/index.tsx`** | **The job.** 35 refs → `footer.ts` parts, following the pattern item 7 established for three elements |
| 5 | — | `rm overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` |

Steps 1–3 and 5 are minutes. **Step 4 is the work** — and it's the same migration item 7 did for `SubscribeModal` and `SubscribeSection`, applied to the remaining elements. `ContactIconRow` is the last footer sub-component still fully inline.

## My honest read on whether to do it now

The strongest argument isn't the drift risk — it's that **the footer is the last place in the PR still styling itself at the call site**, and finishing it closes items 5 and 6 together. Deleting `cssVars.ts` then becomes a consequence rather than a task.

The weakest argument is urgency: 0/91 drifted, so nothing is broken today.

If you want it done, I'd do steps 1–3 now (15 minutes, low risk) and treat step 4 as its own change — it's the larger half of what's left in the footer, and it deserves a reviewable diff of its own rather than being bundled.

Want me to take steps 1–3, the whole thing, or leave it for the branch owner?

## What changed

**Step 1 — five story files.** All `cssVars` imports removed:

```tsx
<Box bg={cssVars.color.background['05']} …>   →  <Box bg="background.05" …>
<Text style={{color: cssVars.color.text.secondary}}>  →  <Text color="text.secondary">
<div style={{backgroundColor: …, padding: …}}>  →  <Box bg="background.05" p="xl">
```

The two `<div>` cases became `<Box>` (imported from Chakra), which also removed four inline styles from the stories.

**Step 2 — `zimmLogo`.** An SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete colour, not a `var()` reference, so `useToken` is the right tool rather than a Chakra prop:

```tsx
const [inverseColour, defaultColour] = useToken('colors', ['text.inverse', 'text.default'])
const fill = variant === 'inverse' ? inverseColour : defaultColour
```

Behaviour is identical — it now resolves through the registered theme instead of a hand-typed mirror. All 10 `<path fill={fill}>` untouched.

**Step 3 — `zimmNavItem`.** This one had a subtlety worth flagging.

The `fontFamily` override was applied via `sx` specifically because **`sx` outranks the `textStyle` prop, and `__css` doesn't.** Moving `fontFamily` into the recipe alone would have let `textStyle="navigation"` win and silently restore the heading font.

So I moved **both** into the recipe, ordered so `fontFamily` overrides the expanded `textStyle`:

```ts
const baseStyle = {
    textStyle: 'navigation',
    fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',   // deliberately overrides the spread
    …
}
```

and dropped `textStyle="navigation"`, `sx={{fontFamily}}` and the `fontOverride` const from both JSX branches. Net effect: the component carries no styling at all now — just `__css={styles}`.

## Where item 6 stands

```
cssVars.ts:  245 lines, 91 vars, 7 text presets
importers:   1  (was 8)
             └─ components/footer/index.tsx — 35 refs
```

Step 4 is the whole remaining job: migrating the footer's 35 references into `footer.ts` parts, following the pattern item 7 established for `SubscribeModal` and `SubscribeSection`. `ContactIconRow` is the last sub-component still fully inline.

Once that's done, step 5 is `rm overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts` — and items 5 and 6 close together.

## What moved

**16 new parts in `footer.ts`** (33 total), grouped by area:

- **Modal** — `modalOverlay`, `modalTitle`, `modalField`, `modalFieldLast`, `modalConsent`, `modalConsentLink`, `modalDisclaimer`, `modalActions`
- **Link columns** — `columnHeading`, `linkList`, `linkListItem`, `contactRow`, `contactIconLink`
- **Bottom bar** — `copyright`, `legalLink`
- **Subscribe** — `subscribeSuccess`

Four module-level style objects deleted (`labelStyle`, `bottomBarTextStyle`, `subscribeSuccessStyle`, `iconLinkStyle`), plus `MODAL_OVERLAY_BG`, `MODAL_TEXT_MUTED` and `MODAL_Z_INDEX` — all now in the recipe. `ContactIconRow` was the last sub-component not consuming the theme; it does now.

## Three judgement calls worth flagging

**1 · I added an `sx` prop to `ZimmNavItem`.** The footer passes styles *into* that component, and its only channel was `style?: CSSProperties` — which takes raw CSS, so Chakra token keys like `'xs'` wouldn't resolve. A three-line `sx?: SystemStyleObject` pass-through lets the footer send `sx={styles.legalLink}` properly. Small API addition to an atom we own, and it's the idiomatic Chakra escape hatch.

**2 · The contact icons now inherit their colour.** `ZimmIcon` already defaults to `color='currentColor'`, so instead of passing `color={cssVars.color.text.inverse}` at three call sites, `contactIconLink` sets `color` once and the glyphs inherit. Same for the locale chevron.

**3 · One inline style remains, deliberately.** It's `<ZimmNavItem style={{whiteSpace:'normal', height:'auto', textTransform:'uppercase'}} />` in the link list — three plain CSS keywords with no token involved. Converting it to `sx` would be churn for no gain.

cssVars.ts   245 lines · 0 importers   ← orphaned, ready to delete
```

**Step 5 is the deletion, and I've deliberately not done it** — AGENTS.md Hard Rule #9 is explicit that files don't get deleted without an explicit ask in the prompt, and you asked for step 4. It's a single command whenever you want it:

```bash
git rm overrides/app/utils/cssVars.ts
```

That closes items 5 and 6 together, and leaves only item 1 (`eslint --fix`) outstanding across the whole list.

One note for whoever reviews: the footer has a `SubscribeSubmit` Storybook `play` test that clicks through the modal. It typechecks, but `vitest` doesn't run `play` functions — worth a `npm run storybook` pass before merge, since the modal's element types changed.

## Confirming it was formatting-only

Three ways, because a 2126-change auto-fix on an uncommitted tree deserves it:

**1 · By construction.** I audited before running: of everything ESLint offered to fix, **2126 of 2126 were `prettier/prettier`** — no other rule provided a fix, so `--fix` had nothing else it could apply.

**2 · By inspection.** The changes are quote spacing, semicolons, indentation (4→2 spaces), and line reflowing:

```diff
- import {useRef, useState} from 'react'
+ import { useRef, useState } from 'react';

-     value?:        string
+   value?: string;
```

My first normalisation check flagged 22 files, which was my test being wrong, not the fix — prettier also changes quotes, semicolons and trailing commas, none of which are whitespace. After normalising those too, only 3 files differed, and inspecting them showed line **re-wrapping** (prettier joining a 3-line `renderHook(...)` call onto one line, reflowing a multi-line import list) — my normaliser couldn't account for that, but the tokens are identical.

The reason it went unnoticed: **there is no lint step in any workflow.** I grepped `.github/workflows/*.yml` — nothing runs `npm run lint` or `eslint`. PR #55's check list confirms it: Tier guards, Vitest, Storybook, Playwright, BrowserStack, CodeRabbit, Deploy Preview — no lint job.

## So, precisely

- **Lint errors in branch-changed files: 0.**

## Two things worth your attention

**Fixing the 19 pre-existing errors is one command** (`npx eslint overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts overrides/app/routes.tsx --fix`) — but both files are outside this PR's scope, and `routes.tsx` is **Tier 2 Global Shell**. Cleaning develop's lint debt inside a footer PR would widen the diff and drag in another squad's file for no functional reason. I'd leave it and raise it separately.

**The bigger finding: lint isn't gated.** That's why 2126 prettier problems could accumulate on a single branch unnoticed, and why `develop` sits red. Adding a lint job to `qa.yml` would have caught this at the first commit — though it's Tier 1 (`.github/workflows/`), so it's a decision rather than a quick fix. Worth adding to the Play 5 list alongside `auditTokenUsage.mjs`; both are the same gap — rules that exist but nothing enforces.

Also visible in that check run: **BrowserStack E2E = FAILURE**, and Storybook + Playwright = CANCELLED. Those predate today's work, but they'll need resolving before merge — and the Storybook job is the one that would exercise the `play` tests I flagged.

**The fix isn't a code change — it's a conversation with Kiera.** Take all eight as one batch with their Figma alias names:

```
alias/size/logo/max-width (327px) · alias/size/logo/height (39px)
alias/space/section (48px) · alias/size/footer/col-width-{nav,subscribe,sitemap}
alias/size/modal/footer (480px) · alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max (200px)
alias/size/field/height (36px)
```

Once confirmed they become `foundation/` entries — a Tier 1 PR, designer-owned — and these eight constants become imports. Until then, leaving them flagged is the correct behaviour, not debt.

---

# 12 · `_firstName` / `_lastName` unused

**Where:** `footer/index.tsx:218`

```tsx
const handleModalSubmit = (_firstName: string, _lastName: string) => {
  // PLACEHOLDER until HPC-036 (Omneo integration) lands.
  // pendingEmailRef.current, _firstName, _lastName are available here for the Omneo POST.
  setModalOpen(false);
  setSubmitState('unavailable');
};
```

**What's wrong: almost nothing.** The underscore prefix already signals deliberate non-use, the comment names the ticket, and the params are kept precisely so the Omneo POST has them when HPC-036 lands. Deleting them would make the eventual integration harder.

**The only real issue is noise** — two warnings that will be scrolled past forever, training people to ignore lint output.

**Three options:**

1. **Accept them.** Zero work. They're honest.
2. **`eslint-disable-next-line` with the ticket reference** — silences them and puts *why* at the point of use.
3. **Configure `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'`** in `.eslintrc.js` — the conventional setting, makes underscore-prefixed args project-wide legal. But `.eslintrc.js` is **Tier 1**, so it's a governance decision, not a quick edit.

I'd take **option 2** here and raise **option 3** separately — the underscore convention is used elsewhere and the rule should match it.

---

# 13 · Preview environment vs Figma — the one I can't do

**This isn't a code item.** It's Play 5's question 8, and it needs a human with the Figma file open.

**What's outstanding:** a side-by-side of the deployed preview against Figma at the defined breakpoints, checking spacing, states and responsive behaviour. Nothing in `tsc`, `vitest`, `eslint` or CodeRabbit covers design parity — `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots, and Play 7 notes design-parity validation has **no automated home and no named owner**.

**Why it matters more than usual now:** this PR changed element types extensively — the footer modal, both subscribe paragraphs, the text input's entire DOM, the nav item. All type-check and test green, but *"renders identically to before"* is not something any gate here proves.

**Two blockers to clear first:**

- The preview URL is on the PR — but the latest check run shows **`Storybook interaction & a11y tests = CANCELLED`** and **`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) = FAILURE`**. The Storybook job is the one that would exercise the `play` functions I've flagged repeatedly.
- Worth running `npm run storybook` locally regardless, since `vitest` never executes `play`.

**Budget an hour**, per the playbook. It's the last review surface, and with ≤10 defects allowed it's the one that catches what everything else structurally cannot.

visual QA pass would sign it off; only clicking reveals it.

## Why it's a defect and not a styling nit

- **AGENTS.md, Rules:** *"No mocking: All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API… No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths."*
- **`.docs/prd/homepage.md:76-81` — HPC-030–033, HPC-038, all Confirmed:** the footer is CMS-driven, and *"Business users can add region-specific footer links — e.g. Acknowledgement of Country on AU storefront"*. A hardcoded fixture makes that requirement unimplementable — and note the fixture already contains the AU-specific "Acknowledgement of Country" link, which would then show on all 8 storefronts.
- Against a **≤10 defect, no-Sev3** budget, dead navigation on every page is not a cosmetic finding.

## The nuance worth being fair about

This wasn't carelessness. The component's own JSDoc says:

> *Contentful fetch, Omneo email submit, and Cookie Settings are separate stories (HPC-034, HPC-035, HPC-038).*

So the fetch was **deliberately scoped out** of SFCC-55, and the default was a bridge to let the component render standalone. The intent is sound; what's wrong is the bridge being load-bearing in production.

---

# How to fix it

## The trap: you can't just delete the default

```tsx
const { subscribeHeading, subscribeBody, navGroups, legalLinks = [], copyrightOwner } = data.fields;
```

`data.fields` is destructured immediately. Remove the default and `<Footer />` from `_app` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fields')` — a white screen on every page. So the fix is two changes, not one.

## Minimum viable — in this PR

**1 · Drop the default, keep the type optional:**

```tsx
export const Footer = ({
- data = FOOTER_FIXTURE,
+ data,
  copyrightYear = new Date().getFullYear(),
  …
}: FooterProps) => {
+ // No live footerConfig yet (HPC-034). Render nothing rather than substituting
+ // placeholder content — a footer of dead '#' links is worse than no footer.
+ if (!data) return null;
  const { subscribeHeading, … } = data.fields;
```

**2 · Remove the `FOOTER_FIXTURE` import** from the component. It stays in `contentfulFixture.ts` for stories and tests, which already pass it explicitly — the JSDoc tells them to, and the stories do.

**3 · Same treatment for `privacyPolicyHref = '#'`** (line 370) — another placeholder default feeding a real anchor in the subscribe modal.

That's ~6 lines, and it converts a silent wrong-content bug into an honest absence.

## The real fix — its own story

Someone has to supply `data`. The pattern already exists in this repo:

- `overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts` — the client hook
- `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx` and `pages/contentfulPreview/index.tsx` — two working consumers to copy

Two options, and this is a genuine architectural choice:

| | Approach | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Override `_app` to fetch `footerConfig` and pass it down | Keeps `Footer` presentational per `components.md`'s container rule. But `_app` is **Tier 2 shared shell** — both squads |
| **B** | A `FooterContainer` that fetches and renders `Footer` | Smaller blast radius. But `_app` renders `Footer` directly, so you'd still override `_app` to swap in the container |

Either way `_app` gets touched, so **A is the more honest option** — fewer moving parts for the same cost.

**That's HPC-034 territory, not SFCC-55.** It needs the Contentful `footerConfig` content type to exist and credentials to be live, both of which are outside this PR.

---

## What I'd do

**Make the minimum-viable change now** — it's small, it's contained, and it removes a production defect from a PR that's otherwise close to mergeable. Then raise the fetch as HPC-034 with the A/B decision attached.

The one thing to check before shipping it: **does `_app` tolerate a null footer?** It renders `<Footer />` inside an `<Island>`, so an empty render should be fine — but that's worth eyeballing in the preview rather than assuming.

Note it *flattened* the tiers in the process — `atoms/` and `molecules/` disappeared here.

## `a7b1586` — the tiers came back

components/ui-kits/{ => molecules}/zimmInputAction/index.tsx

So the path went:

```

overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmButton/index.tsx             9bd13bf
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx       a7b1586  ← current

## Correcting myself

When I first summarised the ten new commits on #55, I attributed the move to `a7b1586` — *"moved to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<camelCase>/index.tsx` — now nested under `components/`"*. That conflated the two. The relocation was `9bd13bf`; `a7b1586` only re-added the tier folders.

## Why it matters

The move under `components/` is what made the structure **registry-visible** — `generateRegistry.mjs` scans `overrides/app/components/`, so at the old top-level path these components were invisible to it. That's also why the registry files show up as modified in both commits.

text:
nfirmed):** Business users can add region-specific footer links — e.g. Acknowledgement of Country on AU storefront

The hrefs aren't developer-known values waiting to be typed in. They're **business-authored content, per storefront, across 8 sites and 11 locales.** Nobody can supply them from code — that's the point of the requirement.

So the `#` values aren't laziness. They're standing in for content that genuinely does not exist yet, and won't until the Contentful story lands.

## 2 · The motivation — and where it goes wrong

The intent is legitimate and documented. The component's JSDoc says the Contentful fetch is a **separate story (HPC-034)**, and the placeholder schema says it'll move to the sync script *"only when that story is scheduled."*

So: build the component now, wire the CMS later. That's correct sequencing — `.claude/rules/components.md`'s container/presentational rule and the manual's **static-first** principle both say exactly this: *"Where an integration isn't available yet, build against static data and move on. Props in, markup out. Static/mock data lives in the story, not in the component."*

**The failure is one word: `not in the component`.**

```tsx
data = FOOTER_FIXTURE,   // ← this is the whole defect
```

Static-first was followed for the *shape* and abandoned for the *binding*. Had the fixture stayed in the story, this would be textbook. Instead the default makes it the production value.

## 3 · What the rules say

Four rules converge, and they all say the same thing:

**AGENTS.md → Rules → No mocking**
> *All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API… No MSW or **hardcoded fixtures in production paths**.*

**AGENTS.md → Requirements**
> *If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for approval**. Do not fill gaps with assumptions.*

**The FED manual, §7 — Raise, don't invent**
> *Silently inventing a value is the failure mode.*

**Mechanically enforced:** `jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid` — *"The href attribute requires a valid value to be accessible… If you cannot provide a valid href, use a button."* This was the one real ESLint error in the PR, and it's since been fixed for the nav items.

**And CodeRabbit said it independently:** *"Do not retain placeholder href values such as `tel:`, `mailto:`, or `#`."*

## The pattern is already in this PR — applied to the wrong half

Commit `e9c2180` solved exactly this problem for the contact icons:

```tsx
href ? (
  <chakra.a href={href} aria-label={label}>…</chakra.a>
) : (
  // No Contentful href yet — render as visible but inert placeholder.
  // <span> without role/tabIndex is not keyboard-reachable and aria-hidden
  <chakra.span aria-hidden={true}>…</chakra.span>
)
```

**That's the correct answer, already written, already reviewed, already in the file.** Absent href → render something inert and honest, never a dead link.

The nav links and `privacyPolicyHref` simply didn't get the same treatment — because they receive their `#` from the *fixture* rather than from absent data, so they never look absent.

## So the fix follows from what's already here

Not "find the real URLs" — they don't exist and aren't ours to know. It's:

1. **Drop `data = FOOTER_FIXTURE`** so absence is visible instead of masked
2. **Apply the `ContactIconRow` pattern** to nav links and the privacy link — inert when there's no destination
3. **Keep the fixture in the stories**, where static-first says it belongs
4. **HPC-034 supplies the real content** when the content type is created and business users author it

The honest framing for the PR thread: *the footer's markup and styling are complete; its content binding is stubbed pending HPC-034, and the stub currently reaches production.* That's a one-line description of a real defect with a known owner — much better than "hardcoded links."

Want me to make that change — the default removal plus extending the inert-placeholder pattern to the nav links?

text:
nual's static-first principle both say build against static data when the integration isn't ready. The fixture is correct, well-shaped, and well-documented.

**The defect is where it's bound.** Static-first says *"static data lives in the story, not in the component."* Binding it as a **default parameter** moves it from the story into the runtime contract — so the placeholder becomes the production value rather than a story-only input.

Three consequences:

1. **It fails silently.** Absent CMS data is indistinguishable from present CMS data. Nothing logs, nothing warns, nothing looks broken — QA signs it off, and only a click reveals it.
2. **It renders AU-specific content globally.** The fixture includes "Acknowledgement of Country". HPC-038 says that's an AU-only, business-authored link. It would appear on all 8 storefronts.
3. **It masks the real gap.** With a working default, nothing forces HPC-034 to be scheduled — the footer *looks* finished.

## How it should be instead

**The pattern is already in this file**, written for the contact icons in commit `e9c2180`:

```tsx
{links.map(({ href, label, icon }) =>
  href ? (
    <chakra.a href={href} aria-label={label}>…</chakra.a>
  ) : (
    // No Contentful href yet — render as visible but inert placeholder.
    // <span> without role/tabIndex is not keyboard-reachable and aria-hidden
    // prevents screen readers from announcing an unnamed interactive control.
    <chakra.span aria-hidden={true}>…</chakra.span>
  ),
)}
```

**Absent destination → render something inert and honest. Never a dead link.**

Applied to the two places that didn't get it:

```tsx
// 1 · absence becomes visible instead of masked
- data = FOOTER_FIXTURE,
- privacyPolicyHref = '#',
+ data,
+ privacyPolicyHref,
+ // No live footerConfig yet (HPC-034). Render nothing rather than substituting
+ // placeholder content — a footer of dead links is worse than no footer.
+ if (!data) return null;

// 2 · per-link, matching ContactIconRow
- <ZimmNavItem href={link.fields.href} label={link.fields.label} inverse … />
+ {link.fields.href
+   ? <ZimmNavItem href={link.fields.href} label={link.fields.label} inverse … />
+   : <chakra.span aria-hidden={true} __css={styles.inertLink}>{link.fields.label}</chakra.span>}
```

The per-link guard matters even after HPC-034 lands — a business user can save a nav link with the label filled and the href blank, and this handles that permanently.

---

## The difference

| | Current | Corrected |
|---|---|---|
| **No CMS data** | 18 links render, all `href="#"` | Footer renders nothing (or an explicit empty state) |
| **Failure mode** | **Silent** — looks complete | **Visible** — obviously unfinished |
| **Clicking a link** | Jumps to top of page, URL gains `#` | Nothing to click |
| **Screen reader** | Announces 18 actionable links that do nothing | Announces static text, or nothing |
| **AU-only content** | "Acknowledgement of Country" on all 8 storefronts | Nothing until a business user authors it per site |
| **Blank href post-HPC-034** | Renders a dead link | Renders inert text |
| **Pressure to schedule HPC-034** | None — it looks done | Immediate — the footer is visibly empty |
| **AGENTS.md "no fixtures in production paths"** | ❌ violated | ✅ satisfied |
| **`jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid`** | passes only because `#` is technically a value | ✅ genuinely satisfied |
| **Stories & tests** | Work (via the default) | Work (pass `FOOTER_FIXTURE` explicitly — already documented in the JSDoc) |

**The single sentence version:** today the component *pretends* it has content; corrected, it *admits* it doesn't — and the fixture goes back to being story-only, which is where static-first says it belongs.

The one deliberate trade-off: on a live storefront today, the footer would disappear entirely rather than show placeholder links. That is the correct outcome — an absent footer is an obvious bug someone fixes, while a footer of dead links is a defect that ships.

sn't exist.** Phase is *Detailed Design*, the only tag is `v0.1.0-rc.0`, go-live is `v1.0.0`. There is no live storefront. Nothing is reaching a customer tomorrow. I called it "🔴 a real defect shipping to production" — that was wrong.

**2 · "Render nothing" was a bad proposal.** It would remove the footer from the **preview environment** — the surface PR #54 exists to provide and that Play 5 names as a required review lens. You'd lose the ability to check the footer against Figma at breakpoints, which is precisely the review that a 10-defect budget makes non-optional. I optimised for a rule and broke the workflow.

## What the facts actually say about testing

Your question — how would the links be tested — has a better answer than I gave:

| Surface | Depends on the default? |
|---|---|
| **Storybook** | ❌ No — `index.stories.tsx:13-14` already sets `args: { data: FOOTER_FIXTURE }` explicitly. Six stories, all pass it |
| **Vitest** | ❌ No footer unit test exists |
| **Playwright** | ❌ No footer E2E spec exists |
| **Preview environment** | ✅ **Yes — this is the only thing that needs it** |

So the stories already comply with static-first. The default exists solely so the **running app** renders a footer. That's a legitimate need, not a shortcut.

## So the current approach is more defensible than I said

Static-first says *"build against static data and move on, don't block."* The dependency here is genuinely pending — `footerConfig` doesn't exist as a content type, and the destinations are business-authored per storefront. Blocking the UI build on that would be exactly the failure the principle exists to prevent.

**The one real weakness stands:** a default that works everywhere is the kind of thing that survives to launch unnoticed. That's a *tracking* problem, not a code defect.

And the "proper" fix — overriding `_app` to pass `data={FOOTER_FIXTURE}` — means copy-first on a **503-line Tier 2 file** that we don't currently override. That's disproportionate today, and HPC-034 has to do it anyway.

## Revised recommendation

**Keep the default.** Change three things instead:

**1 · Add the per-link `href` guard.** This is worth doing regardless of HPC-034, and it costs nothing:

```tsx
{link.fields.href
  ? <ZimmNavItem href={link.fields.href} label={link.fields.label} inverse … />
  : <chakra.span aria-hidden={true} __css={styles.inertLink}>{link.fields.label}</chakra.span>}
```

Why it survives the integration: **a business user can save a nav link with a label and a blank href.** The guard protects against that permanently, and it matches `ContactIconRow` — the pattern already reviewed and merged in this same file. Same for `privacyPolicyHref`.

**2 · Name the temporariness at the binding**, so it reads as scheduled rather than settled:

```tsx
// TEMPORARY (HPC-034): the app has no footerConfig source yet, so the component
// defaults to the fixture in order to render in dev/preview. Remove this default
// when the CDA fetch lands — stories pass `data` explicitly and don't rely on it.
data = FOOTER_FIXTURE,
```

**3 · Track it as a launch blocker, not a code comment.** Add it to `projectState.md`'s *Unresolved Dependencies* — the section that exists exactly for "don't hard-code assumptions about this." A comment gets read by whoever opens the file; that list gets read at every session start.

## Revised severity

**🔴 → 🟡 Tracked temporary binding**, with one genuine sub-item (the missing `href` guard) that's worth fixing now.

The thing I'd still flag to you as lead: **the footer has no E2E and no unit test at all.** Six Storybook stories cover it visually, but nothing asserts the links render, point somewhere, or degrade when a destination is missing. When HPC-034 lands and real content flows in, that gap is what will let a regression through — and it's a bigger risk than the fixture default ever was.

Want me to make the two changes — the `href` guard and the temporariness comment — and leave the default in place?

## None of the three patterns are reachable today

The fixture supplies **every** field — 18 hrefs, all headings, body copy, copyright owner. And `'#'` **passes** `SAFE_HREF_RE`, so all 18 render as real `<a href="#">` anchors.

So what QA sees on the preview environment right now:

|---|---|---|---|
| All 18 nav links | ✅ | ✅ real `<a>` | Jump to top of page |
| Legal links | ✅ | ✅ | Jump to top |

I was describing failure modes that are currently unreachable, and I should have checked that before ranking them.

## So your three QA concerns, precisely

**"Missing or unrendered components"** — doesn't happen today. It *would* have happened under my earlier "render nothing" proposal, which is exactly why you were right to reject it.

**"Clickable elements that aren't clickable"** — doesn't happen today. Every link is a real anchor.

**"Expected behaviour missing"** — this one *is* live, but it's a single, well-defined item: **links navigate to `#` instead of a destination.** That's not a bug in the code; it's the absence of HPC-034.

## Which means the real risk is an AC gap, not a code gap

If QA tests SFCC-55 against Figma with no statement about data state, they'll raise ~18 defects for "link does not navigate." Against a 10-defect budget that's catastrophic — and every one would be invalid.

**The fix is in the story, not the component.** SFCC-55's AC needs an explicit line:

> Footer content is supplied by a static fixture pending **HPC-034** (Contentful `footerConfig`). Nav, legal and contact links render and are focusable but navigate to `#`. Destination correctness is **out of scope** for this story and is tested under HPC-034.

That converts 18 would-be defects into one known limitation. Worth raising with Jas now — it's the cheapest defect prevention available, and it's the same "wrong information on the card" problem from Play 8.

I'd also check whether the `.feature` file exists for SFCC-55. There's a Playwright spec for SFCC-89 but I found **no footer E2E at all**, so QA has no automated baseline for it either.

## What the three patterns are actually for

They're not today's defects — they're **HPC-034's** defects, arriving the moment real per-locale content lands:

| Pattern | Triggers when | QA would see |
|---|---|---|
| ② empty fallback | A locale omits `subscribeHeading`/`body` | ~64px blank space above the form |
| ③ silent swap | A business user saves a link with a blank href | Link that looks right, does nothing, announced as a button |
| ① guard + inert | *(already correct)* | — |

HPC-030/038 explicitly allow per-locale variation across 8 storefronts, so partially-populated entries aren't an edge case — they're the expected state.

**And here's the part that matters for your budget:** fixing them now costs nothing visible. Both changes are **invisible against the fixture** — QA sees no difference today, because neither path is reachable. They only start paying off when real content arrives.

Fix them now and they're free. Fix them after HPC-034 and each one arrives as a QA-raised defect first.

## What I'd recommend

1. **Get the AC line into SFCC-55** — highest value, zero code, prevents ~18 invalid defects
2. **Fix pattern ③ in `ZimmNavItem`** — one atom, invisible today, prevents a real a11y defect later
3. **Fix pattern ②'s three cases** — same reasoning
4. **Leave the fixture default alone**, tracked as agreed
5. **Flag to Lead QA that the footer has no `.feature` and no E2E** — that's the gap that lets an HPC-034 regression through

's placement of Contact Us *"remains design-dependent and will follow the new UX designs"* — so it isn't confirmed either.

So the contact icons aren't waiting on a dependency that's specified-but-unbuilt. **They're waiting on a dependency that hasn't been designed.**

## Would activating them be problematic?

**Yes — and more than for the nav links.** Three reasons, in order of weight.

**1 · The failure mode is materially worse.** Nav links use `href="#"`, so a click is a no-op scroll. Contact icons would use `tel:` and `mailto:` — and `SAFE_HREF_RE` permits both. On mobile, a placeholder `tel:` **opens the dialer with a junk number**; `mailto:` opens the mail client. That's not "does nothing", it's "does something wrong and hands the user off to another app."

**2 · Activating them would announce a capability that doesn't exist.** A screen reader would say *"Call us, link"* and *"WhatsApp, link"*. WCAG 2.4.4 (Link Purpose) and 3.2.4 (Consistent Identification) both treat that as a failure — the accessible name promises an action the control can't perform. The current `aria-hidden` span is deliberately silent instead of deliberately misleading.

**3 · It would hide the gap.** Once they "work", nobody notices that `footerConfig` has no contact fields. HPC-034 would ship the Contentful integration and the icons would keep pointing nowhere — because there's no field to populate. The inert state is the only thing currently signalling that this is unfinished.

## Where the current code is genuinely wrong

Not that the icons are inert — that's right. It's `aria-hidden={true}`.

The icons communicate real information: *"Zimmermann has phone, WhatsApp and email support."* Hiding that from screen readers means those users lose content sighted users can see — a 1.1.1 concern. The comment's reasoning (avoid announcing an unnamed interactive control) is sound; the implementation over-corrects by hiding the *content* along with the *affordance*.

Better: keep them non-interactive, but let them be perceivable.

```tsx
href ? (
  <chakra.a href={href} aria-label={label}>
    <ZimmIcon type={icon} />
  </chakra.a>
) : (
  // No destination yet (footerConfig has no contact fields — see HPC-034 / UX).
  // Non-interactive: not focusable, not announced as a control — but the icon's
  // meaning is still exposed, so SR users aren't shown less than sighted users.
  <chakra.span __css={styles.contactIconLink}>
    <ZimmIcon type={icon} aria-hidden={false} role="img" aria-label={label} />
  </chakra.span>
)
```

Same visual, same non-clickability, but *"Call us, image"* instead of silence. No false affordance, no lost information.

## So, three options ranked

| | Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Leave inert, fix the `aria-hidden` over-correction | ✅ **Recommended** — honest, accessible, keeps the gap visible |
| **B** | Give them `#` like the nav links | ⚠️ Consistent with nav links, but announces a non-existent action. Only defensible if the AC covers it |
| **C** | Give them real `tel:`/`mailto:`/`wa.me` values | ❌ Hands users to a dialer with a fake number. Worst option |

**The QA problem you're worried about isn't solved by activating them — it's solved by the AC.** Whether they're inert or fake-active, QA needs to be told which. Option A plus one AC line costs nothing and leaves the code honest:

> Footer contact icons render non-interactive. `footerConfig` has no contact-channel fields defined and footer contact placement is not yet confirmed by UX (see homepage.md HPC-018 note). Out of scope for SFCC-55.

**And there's a real backlog item underneath this**, which is the more valuable finding: the contact icons are built and styled against a content model that doesn't include them. Someone needs to either add `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref` to `footerConfig`, or confirm with UX that the icons belong in the footer at all. That's worth raising with Jas and Kiera before HPC-034 gets scheduled, because it changes the schema.

text:
Let me check `ZimmIcon`'s actual API before I explain the mechanics, since my suggestion depends on it.

`ZimmIcon` already handles this properly — a discriminated union forcing you to choose *either* `aria-hidden: true` *or* `aria-label`, and it sets `role="img"` automatically when labelled. So the mechanism I described is already built into the atom; the footer just isn't using it.

## The idea: interactivity and perceivability are separate axes

They get conflated because on a working link they arrive together. They don't have to.

| | Interactive | Perceivable |
|---|---|---|
| Can you click it? | ✅ | — |
| Can you Tab to it? | ✅ | — |
| Does a screen reader announce it exists? | — | ✅ |
| Does it say what it *is*? | — | ✅ |
| Does it promise an *action*? | ✅ | ❌ |

Today's code sets **both to off**. My suggestion is to turn only the second one on.

## What changes concretely

**Now** — `aria-hidden={true}`:

```tsx
<chakra.span aria-hidden={true}>
  <ZimmIcon type="phone" size="md" aria-hidden={true} />
</chakra.span>
```

- Sighted user: sees a phone icon
- Screen reader user: **hears nothing at all** — the element is removed from the accessibility tree
- Keyboard: skipped
- Click: nothing

**Proposed** — labelled instead of hidden:

```tsx
<chakra.span __css={styles.contactIconLink}>
  <ZimmIcon type="phone" size="md" aria-label="Call us" />
</chakra.span>
```

`ZimmIcon` then emits `role="img" aria-label="Call us"`.

- Sighted user: **identical** — same icon, same size, same position
- Screen reader user: hears **"Call us, image"**
- Keyboard: still skipped — a `<span>` has no tabindex
- Click: still nothing

**Nothing visual changes. Nothing becomes clickable.** The only difference is that screen-reader users stop getting less information than everyone else.

## Why that's the right shape here

The icons carry real, true information: *Zimmermann offers phone, WhatsApp and email contact.* That's worth conveying. What isn't true yet is *"and you can start that from here."*

- `aria-hidden` denies the information → 1.1.1 (Non-text Content) concern
- A `<a href="#">` or `<button>` promises the action → 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 concern
- `role="img"` + label conveys the information without promising the action → neither

## Being straight about the trade-off

This isn't unambiguously correct — it's the best of three imperfect options.

**The honest objection:** announcing "Call us, image" is slightly odd. A screen-reader user is told a contact channel exists and given no way to use it. That's a mild consistency wrinkle.

**The fully-correct answer** would be not rendering them until there's a destination — but you've already ruled that out for good reason: QA sees a missing component, and the build is static-first.

So the ranking, given the constraint:

| | Sighted | Screen reader | False affordance | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hidden *(now)* | icon | **nothing** | no | ⚠️ information loss |
| **Labelled image** | icon | "Call us, image" | no | ✅ **best available** |
| `href="#"` | icon | "Call us, link" | **yes** | ❌ |
| Real `tel:` | icon | "Call us, link" | opens dialer | ❌ |

## What it means for your QA concern

It doesn't fully solve it — a QA engineer clicking the icon still gets nothing, and will still raise it without an AC line. What it does do is make the **a11y audit** clean: an accessibility reviewer running axe or NVDA would currently flag three icons missing from the accessibility tree. After this, they wouldn't.

Given WCAG 2.2 AA is the target and a11y findings count against the same defect budget, that's worth the two-line change on its own.

The change is: drop `aria-hidden={true}` from both the wrapper span and the icon, pass `aria-label={label}` instead. `ZimmIcon`'s type union already enforces that you do exactly one or the other, so it can't be got half-right.

Want me to make it?

Plus the exit condition — switch to the `<a>` branch when a real href arrives.

That should be settled **before** HPC-034 is scheduled, because it changes the schema — and `contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts` is the file that would need updating.

as a **fully working** locale selector:

```jsx
const [locale, setLocale] = useState(intl.locale)
const {site, buildUrl} = useMultiSite()
const supportedLocaleIds = site.l10n?.supportedLocales.map((l) => l.id)
const showLocaleSelector = supportedLocaleIds?.length > 1        // ← line 42

{showLocaleSelector && (
  <Select defaultValue={locale} onChange={({target}) => {
    setLocale(target.value)
    const newUrl = getPathWithLocale(target.value, buildUrl, {disallowParams: ['refine']})
    window.location = basePath ? `${basePath}${newUrl}` : newUrl   // ← actually navigates
  }} aria-label={intl.formatMessage({id: 'footer.locale_selector.assistive_msg'})}>
    {supportedLocaleIds.map((locale) => <option …><LocaleText shortCode={locale} /></option>)}
  </Select>
)}
```

Every piece we said was "waiting on a dependency" already exists and works:

| Need | Status |
|---|---|
| Current locale | ✅ `intl.locale` |
| Available locales | ✅ `site.l10n.supportedLocales` |
| Switching behaviour | ✅ `getPathWithLocale` + navigate |
| Accessible name | ✅ `footer.locale_selector.assistive_msg`, all 11 locales |
| E2E hook | ✅ `data-testid="sf-footer-locale-selector"` |
| **HPC-026's AU exception** | ✅ **`supportedLocaleIds?.length > 1`** — AU has one locale, so it hides itself |

That last row is the striking one. The PRD requirement — *"selector appears in the footer on all storefronts except AU"* — is already satisfied by base logic we removed.

## So this isn't the same as the contact icons

| | Contact icons | Locale button |
|---|---|---|
| Data source | `footerConfig` — **field doesn't exist** | `useMultiSite()` — **available now** |
| UX confirmed? | ❌ "design-dependent" | ✅ HPC-026 confirmed |
| Base capability | none | ✅ **working, and we replaced it** |
| Correct resolve | inert + perceivable | **restore the behaviour** |

It also breaches AGENTS.md's *Minimal changes* rule directly: *"Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed."* The Figma redesign instructed a change of **appearance**, not a removal of **function**.

## The resolve

**Restyle the base selector — don't reimplement it.**

Keep the Figma appearance (text + chevron, `styles.localeButton`, `styles.localeText`) and put the base's logic behind it:

```tsx
const intl = useIntl();
const {site, buildUrl} = useMultiSite();
const supportedLocaleIds = site.l10n?.supportedLocales.map((l) => l.id) ?? [];
if (supportedLocaleIds.length <= 1) return null;   // HPC-026: no selector on AU
```

Then either drive the existing button from a `<Select>`/menu, or — lowest risk — render the base `<Select>` visually styled via `footer.ts` so the switching logic stays untouched.

**Three things that fall out for free:**
- AU stops showing a selector, per HPC-026
- The label becomes the *actual* locale instead of hardcoded "United States (USD) / ENG" on all 8 storefronts
- `data-testid="sf-footer-locale-selector"` returns, so QA gets a stable selector

## Where it should be done

**Not in this PR.** It's real behaviour with multi-site implications across 8 storefronts and 11 locales, and it needs its own QA pass. It should be a story with HPC-026 attached.

**But it changes how you describe it.** "Locale selector not yet wired" understates it — the honest line is *"SFCC-55 replaced the working base locale selector with a non-functional styled button; restoring it is tracked under HPC-026."* That's a regression against confirmed functionality, and it's the kind of thing that quietly ships if it's filed as an unbuilt feature.

## Interim, if the story can't land in this PR

Make it stop lying, exactly as we did for the contact icons — a `<span>` with the locale text and chevron, no `type="button"`, no `aria-label`, nothing focusable. It's still wrong content on 7 of 8 storefronts, but it stops announcing an action it can't perform.

**Two-line change; I can do it now if you want the interim state.** The restore itself I'd scope as its own story.

## Why "restore the base selector" was wrong

Two facts I hadn't verified:

**1 · Every one of the 11 sites has exactly one locale.**

```
ZimmermannAU  ["en"]      ZimmermannUS    ["en-US"]    ZimmermannUK  ["en-GB"]
ZimmermannEUfr ["fr"]     ZimmermannEUit  ["it"]       ZimmermannHK  ["en-HK"]   …
```

The base gate is `showLocaleSelector = supportedLocaleIds?.length > 1`. Restoring it would render **nothing on any storefront** — not just AU. So the "AU exception comes free" claim I made was wrong; it hides everywhere for the same reason.

**2 · HPC-026 isn't asking for a locale selector.** `regional.md` REG-020 – REG-027 describes something substantially bigger:

> **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU. Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) **with currency display and search field** (REG-021). **Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag** (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES (REG-023). **China → HK** (REG-026). **Australia from another storefront → HK** (REG-027).

That's a **cross-storefront country/region switcher** with grouped regions, search, currency display, a basket-loss warning, and two special routing rules. The base `LocaleSelector` is a language dropdown *within* one site. Different component, different problem.

**So it isn't a regression after all.** The base capability doesn't do what Zimmermann needs, and wouldn't render. I called it "the worst implemented" and "a regression against confirmed functionality" — that was wrong on both counts, and it was based on my not checking `sites.js`.

## What it actually is

A genuinely unbuilt feature with confirmed requirements — REG-020 through REG-027, plus REG-014–019 for the related mismatch slide-out. It needs:

- A cross-site country list grouped by region, with search and currency
- The REG-022 basket-loss warning
- REG-026 / REG-027 routing exceptions
- URL locale reflection for EU (REG-024)

That is a story, not a fix. And `.docs/prd/homepage.md` notes *"No international pages exist yet (HPC-026 design note)"* — the design isn't there either.

## So the resolve I'd now recommend

**Same treatment as the contact icons: make it stop lying, and don't build it here.**

```tsx
// Country/region selector (REG-020–REG-027) is a separate story: cross-storefront
// switching, region grouping, currency display, search, and the REG-022 basket-loss
// warning. The base LocaleSelector is a within-site *language* dropdown and does not
// apply — every Zimmermann site has exactly one locale, so it would never render.
// Non-interactive until that story lands: no button semantics, nothing focusable,
// nothing announced as a control. Label is still hardcoded — see below.
<chakra.span __css={styles.localeButton}>
  <chakra.span __css={styles.localeText}>United States (USD) / ENG</chakra.span>
  <ZimmIcon type="chevron-right" size="sm" aria-hidden={true} />
</chakra.span>
```

That removes the false affordance — no `type="button"`, no `aria-label="Change locale"`, not focusable, not announced.

**One thing it does not fix:** the label is hardcoded "United States (USD) / ENG" and would be wrong on 10 of 11 storefronts. That *is* derivable today from `useMultiSite()` — `site.l10n.defaultCurrency` and `supportedLocales[0].id` are right there. I could make the text correct even while the control stays inert.

So before I write anything, one call for you:

**(a)** Inert only — remove the button semantics, leave the hardcoded label, ticket the rest.
**(b)** Inert **and** derive the label from `useMultiSite()`, so each storefront shows its own country/currency/language while the selector itself waits for REG-020.

**(b) is barely more work** and removes a wrong-content defect QA would otherwise raise on every non-US storefront. I'd go with (b) — but it's your call, since it's slightly beyond "stop the lie".

| Announced as a control | "Change locale, button" | ✅ nothing |
| Keyboard focusable | yes, Enter does nothing | ✅ not focusable |
| Clicking | nothing | nothing (but no longer looks clickable) |
| **Label correctness** | wrong on 10/11 | ❌ **still wrong on 10/11** |

So it closes the accessibility defect and leaves a content defect untouched.

## What QA raises

Against a ≤10 defect budget, **this is worse than the a11y issue it fixes.**

A QA engineer testing the French storefront sees a footer that says *"United States (USD) / ENG"* on a site priced in EUR with French copy. That reads as a live localisation bug, not a placeholder — nothing about it signals "unbuilt". It'd likely be raised as **Sev2**: wrong currency/country indication on a commerce site is the kind of thing that erodes trust and gets escalated.

And it's raised **once per storefront tested** — so multi-region QA generates up to 10 instances of the same finding.

Option B's derived label costs perhaps 5 extra lines:

```tsx
const {site} = useMultiSite();
const {id: localeId, preferredCurrency} = site.l10n.supportedLocales[0];
```

…and every storefront shows its own truth. The control still doesn't open anything — that's REG-020's job — but nothing on screen is *false*.

## The one caveat on B

The Figma label format is "Country (CUR) / LANG". `site.l10n` gives you the locale id (`fr`, `en-HK`) and currency (`EUR`, `USD`) — but **not a country display name**. You'd need a mapping, and `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` already exists in the repo, so the data is likely there.

If that mapping turns out to be missing or ambiguous, the honest fallback is showing what we *do* know — e.g. `EUR / FR` — and flagging the country-name format for Kiera rather than inventing one.

**My recommendation stands: option B.** A is a strictly worse outcome for your defect budget than the problem it solves.

Want me to check `countries.ts` and execute B?

untries.ts` is well-built and has real data — `COUNTRIES` keyed by URL slug, generated from live SCAPI config:

```ts
au:      { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannAU',    locale: 'en',    currency: 'AUD' }
us:      { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannUS',    locale: 'en-US', currency: 'USD' }
'fr-eu': { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU',    locale: 'fr',    currency: 'EUR' }
```

Against the target label **`United States (USD) / ENG`**:

| Part | Derivable? | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Currency `(USD)` | ✅ | `site.l10n.defaultCurrency` or `CountryConfig.currency` |
| Language `ENG` | ✅ | `CountryConfig.locale` → language subtag |
| **Country `United States`** | ❌ | **No display-name field anywhere** |

`CountryConfig` has `urlSlug`, `sfccSiteId`, `locale`, `currency`, `shippingCountry`, `checkoutOwner`, `globalEPricing`, `boutiqueRegion` — **no human-readable name**. And `config/sites.js` site objects carry only `id` and `l10n`.

## Three blockers, in order

**1 · No country display name exists.** `shippingCountry` is an ISO alpha-2 code (`US`, `AU`), not "United States". You'd need a code→name map that doesn't exist, and it'd need translating across 11 locales — Figma shows the country in the site's own language, so the French storefront presumably says *"France"*, not *"France"* in English.

**2 · Site → country isn't 1:1.** `ZimmermannEU` serves `en-eu`, `fr-eu`, `it-eu`, `es-eu` — four slugs, one SFCC site. And `ZimmermannHK` covers 29 destination countries per REG-051. So "which country am I on" isn't answerable from the site alone.

**3 · The displayed country is *selected*, not derived.** REG-020–028 make this explicit: the country selector sets the shipping destination, Global-e locks it at checkout, and changing it may empty the basket. So the footer label is meant to reflect **user-selected state that the selector owns** — the very thing that isn't built.

`fr` and `it` are the clearest proof: no region subtag at all, so there is nothing to derive a country from.

## What B could honestly deliver

A reduced label using only verified data:

| Storefront | Full Figma format | Derivable today |
|---|---|---|
| AU | Australia (AUD) / ENG | **AUD / EN** |
| UK | United Kingdom (GBP) / ENG | **GBP / EN** |
| EU-fr | France (EUR) / FRA | **EUR / FR** |
| HK | Hong Kong (USD) / ENG | **USD / EN** |

Correct on all 11, but **not the Figma design** — it drops the country, which is the most prominent element.

## Revised options

| | Result | Cost | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** — inert, keep hardcoded label | Wrong country + currency on 10/11 | 2 lines | ~10 QA defects, likely Sev2 |
| **B-full** — Figma format, derived | Not possible | — | Needs a country-name map and the selector's state |
| **B-reduced** — `EUR / FR` | Correct everywhere, **off-design** | ~8 lines | 1 QA finding: "label doesn't match Figma" |
| **C** — inert + no label | Correct by omission | 3 lines | 1 QA finding: "text missing vs Figma" |

**B-full is not feasible.** So the real choice is between one *wrong-content* defect per storefront (A) and one *design-deviation* finding overall (B-reduced or C).

## My recommendation

**B-reduced**, with the deviation flagged in-code and taken to Kiera:

```tsx
// Country name is NOT derivable: CountryConfig has no display-name field, ZimmermannEU
// serves 4 slugs, and per REG-020–028 the displayed country reflects the user's
// *selected* shipping destination — state the unbuilt selector owns. Showing currency
// and language only, both verified from site config. Figma format
// "Country (CUR) / LANG" pending the selector story + a country-name source (Kiera).
```

Wrong data is a defect; incomplete-but-true data with a flagged reason is a known limitation. Against a 10-defect budget those are very different things.

But this is now a design deviation as much as a code decision — so if you'd rather hold the Figma format and take the hardcoded label as an explicitly AC-covered placeholder, that's defensible too. **Which way do you want it?**

text:
It doesn't — and that's worth unpicking, because your instinct is pointing at something real.

## Nothing functional is being removed

The current handler is literally:

```tsx
onClick={undefined}
```

Click it today: nothing. Tab to it and press Enter: nothing. There is no behaviour to lose.

What option A removes are **four promises**, not four features:

| Removed | What it was promising |
|---|---|
| `type="button"` + `aria-label` | *"I am a control you can operate"* |
| `cursor: pointer` | *"click me"* |
| `_focusVisible` | *"I'm a keyboard stop worth landing on"* |
| `onClick={undefined}` | nothing at all |

So it reads like a downgrade — `<button>` → `<span>` looks like losing something — but the button was a costume.

## And the information survives

This is the part that makes A coherent rather than destructive. The visible text is real content:

```tsx
<chakra.span __css={styles.localeText}>United States (USD) / ENG</chakra.span>
```

A screen reader traversing the footer still reads that. So after A:

| | Before | After A |
|---|---|---|
| Screen reader hears | *"Change locale, button"* | *"United States (USD) / ENG"* |
| Sighted user sees | the text + chevron | **identical** |
| Keyboard user | lands on it, Enter does nothing | walks past it |

Arguably the *after* is more useful — it announces what's actually on screen instead of a capability that doesn't exist.

## Where you're right to be uneasy

Two things genuinely bother me about A, and neither was in my earlier pitch:

**1 · The chevron still lies.** `chevron-right` is a "this opens something" signal. Removing the cursor, focus ring and role kills the *semantic* affordance but leaves the *visual* one. A sighted user still reads it as tappable. Removing the chevron would fix that — and deviate from Figma.

**2 · Nothing automated would have caught the original anyway.** I should be straight: axe and `@storybook/addon-a11y` flag missing names, contrast, roles — **not** "button with no handler". So this isn't a CI-gate fix. It's a judgement call about honesty, not a failing check being made to pass.

## Which puts a third option on the table

**Option 0 — change nothing, declare everything.**

If the AC already says the control is non-functional and the label is a placeholder, then QA won't raise it, no automated gate fails, and the `<button>` stays for the eventual selector to hang off. When REG-020 lands, you add `onClick` and it's done — no re-markup.

| | A | 0 |
|---|---|---|
| Functional behaviour | none | none |
| QA defects (with AC) | 0 | 0 |
| Automated a11y | passes | passes |
| Screen reader | reads the text | announces a button that does nothing |
| Keyboard | skipped | tab stop that does nothing |
| Work when REG-020 lands | re-add button markup | add `onClick` |
| Honesty | ✅ | ❌ |

**A's only real advantage is that it doesn't mislead an actual user** — someone tabbing the footer with a screen reader on a live preview. That's not nothing, but it's smaller than I implied when I called this "the worst implemented."

So: A costs a little rework later and buys honesty for assistive-tech users. 0 costs nothing and keeps a small lie behind an AC declaration.

Given you've already decided the label stays wrong-but-declared, **0 is more internally consistent** — you'd be declaring both problems rather than fixing one and declaring the other. I'd still lean A for the keyboard/SR experience, but I don't think it's clear-cut, and I over-sold it earlier by calling it a regression against working functionality when it wasn't.

Your call — which way?

---

## 🟡 Two value-duplicates where *footer.ts is the more correct one*

| footer.ts | zimmTokens.ts | Same value? |
|---|---|---|
| `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` | `--zimm-scale-1200: '48px'` | yes — 48px |
| `SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem'` | `--zimm-scale-3500: '140px'` | yes — 140px |

Both pairs are physically identical at default root size, but they **diverge under browser zoom / user font-size** — `rem` scales, `px` doesn't. Per `overrideStyling.md`'s Units rule, spacing must be `rem` for WCAG 1.4.4. So `footer.ts` has it right and the foundation token has it wrong.

I'd **not** collapse these into the existing vars — that would be swapping correct behaviour for incorrect. The fix is to document the relationship and push the unit correction upstream:

```diff
- const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'; // alias/space/section (48px)
+ // alias/space/section (48px). Same value as --zimm-scale-1200, which is '48px'
+ // — kept as rem here for WCAG 1.4.4 zoom scaling. Collapse to the var once
+ // zimmTokens.ts's numeric aliases move to rem (Kiera / Tier 1).
+ const SPACE_SECTION = '3rem';
```

Note this also contradicts `overrideStyling.md`, which claims the 7 numeric aliases are *"not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to derive them from."* Two of them now have exact twins. That doc line needs updating — but it's Tier 1 governance, so it's a flag, not an edit.

---

## ⚪ The 9 genuine gaps — the actual Kiera ask

| Constant | Value | Figma alias claimed | What's missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BP.tabletWide` | 860px | `alias/breakpoint/tablet-wide` | no equivalent in `gridSystem` |
| `BP.desktop` | 1024px | `alias/breakpoint/desktop` | **conflicts** — Chakra `lg`=992px, `xl`=1280px |
| `SIZE_COL_SUB` | 320px | `alias/size/footer/col-width-subscribe` | no width scale exists at all |
| `SIZE_COL_MAP` | 600px | `alias/size/footer/col-width-sitemap` | ″ |
| `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` | 480px | `alias/size/modal/footer` | ″ |
| `SIZE_SUB_BODY_MAX` | 200px | `alias/size/footer/subscribe-body-max` | ″ |
| `COLOUR_HALF_INV` | `rgba(255,255,255,.5)` | `alias/color/opacity-50-inverse` | `colour.opacity` exists but **grey-900 only** — no white twin |
| `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` | 36px | `alias/size/field/height` | no field-height token |
| `OPACITY_DISABLED` | `0.4` | — | no numeric opacity scale |

Two of these are cheap wins worth calling out to her specifically:

- **`COLOUR_HALF_INV`** — `colour.ts:32-36` already has `opacity: {50, 40, 30, 15}` in grey-900. The ask is just *"add the inverse twin"*, mirroring existing structure rather than inventing one.
- **`BP.desktop`** — this is a **conflict, not a gap**. Figma says desktop = 1024px; Chakra's `lg` is 992px and `xl` is 1280px. Someone has to decide whether Figma's 1024 maps onto `lg`, or whether the foundation gains a real 1024 breakpoint. Every footer `@media (min-width: 64em)` is currently unreachable via Chakra responsive props, which is why the file uses raw `@media` throughout.

---

## One more thing

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` tells you to run this before any PR touching `theme/components/**`:

```
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

**It doesn't exist.** `scripts/` has no such file. So the documented pre-PR check for exactly this class of problem has never run — which is a fair part of why 13 literals accumulated without anyone noticing.

---

## Proposed split

| | Action | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Now, this PR** | z-index → `overlay`/`modal`; `BP.tablet` → import; comment the 2 unit-conflicts | nothing |
| **Raise to Kiera** | the 9-row table above | design decision |
| **Backlog** | write `auditTokenUsage.mjs`; correct the `overrideStyling.md` "not duplicates" line | Tier 1 governance |

text:
Let me trace one more link in the chain — whether the values actually arrive non-empty.

They're real customer data — not scaffolding. Here's the full chain:

## The flow

**1 · Footer email field** (HPC-034) — user types their email, hits Subscribe:

```tsx
const handleEmailSubmit = (email: string) => {
  pendingEmailRef.current = email;   // captured
  setModalOpen(true);                // modal opens
};
```

**2 · Modal collects the names** (HPC-035) — two working `ZimmTextInput` fields:

```tsx
<ZimmTextInput label="First Name" name="firstName" />
<ZimmTextInput label="Last Name"  name="lastName" />
```

I verified `name` is forwarded to the real `<input>` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:78`), so these are genuine named form controls, not decorative.

**3 · Form submit reads them out of the DOM:**

```tsx
const handleFormSubmit = (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const firstName = (form.elements.namedItem('firstName') as HTMLInputElement)?.value ?? '';
  const lastName  = (form.elements.namedItem('lastName')  as HTMLInputElement)?.value ?? '';
  onSubmit(firstName.trim(), lastName.trim());   // ← trimmed, real values
};
```

**4 · And then they're dropped:**

```tsx
const handleModalSubmit = (_firstName: string, _lastName: string) => {
  setModalOpen(false);
  setSubmitState('unavailable');   // params never touched
};
```

## What they're *for*

`.docs/prd/homepage.md` §6, both **confirmed** requirements:

> - On clicking the Continue CTA, a **modal** collects the customer's **first name and last name** (HPC-035, confirmed)
> - Sign-up data passed to **Omneo**, which then forwards to **Emarsys** (HPC-036, confirmed)

So `_firstName` + `_lastName` + `pendingEmailRef.current` are the **three fields of the HPC-036 sign-up payload**. That's the whole newsletter registration record. The plumbing is complete — capture, modal, validation, trim, handoff — right up to the final step, where there's no Omneo client to hand them to.

## Why the naming is the actual problem

The `_` prefix conventionally means *"this parameter exists only to satisfy a signature; ignore it."* That's what it's saying here. But it's false:

| | What `_` implies | What's true |
|---|---|---|
| Origin | signature filler | user-typed PII |
| Requirement | none | HPC-035, confirmed |
| Future | may never be used | required by HPC-036 |
| Value | irrelevant | the entire payload |

Someone skimming this reads two throwaway args. It's actually the most important data in the component.

Worth noting the discard itself is **correct**: nothing is logged, nothing is persisted, and `submitState` goes to `'unavailable'` rather than `'success'` — so the user is told plainly it didn't go through. No false promise, no orphaned PII. That part of the state machine is doing exactly the right thing.

The only issue is that the signature lies about what these are.

---

So the question for 12a becomes narrower than I framed it: not *"how do we silence a lint warning"* but **"how do we stop this reading as disposable?"** Dropping the params is one answer. Naming them properly and configuring `argsIgnorePattern` is the other — it keeps the payload shape visible at the signature.

Want me to lay out those two against each other before you pick?

When Kiera lands the real token in `foundation/`, `ZimmTokensGlobal` publishes it at `:root` — and closing the local is **deleting one line**. Every consuming line already reads the final name.

⚠️ **The risk this creates, and why the audit script becomes mandatory:** a component-scoped custom property *overrides* the inherited `:root` value. So a local left behind after the real token lands would **silently shadow it** — the component keeps the placeholder while the rest of the app moves on. That's a worse failure than today's, and it's invisible. It's only safe with a mechanical leftover check.

Also note: **no Tier 2 file declares a `--zimm-*` var today.** This would be a new pattern — worth a deliberate decision with Tim, not something to slide in.
