text:
Validator 2 is in, and it caught something I dismissed earlier today.

Tree clean, back to 185. Validator 2 confirmed all five — and corrected me three times.

## The one I got wrong by dismissing it

`header/index.tsx:302` — `fontSize="l"`. Phase 1's category 1b flagged **exactly this line**, every run, and I classified it *"pre-existing, not ours"* and moved on.

```
theme.fontSizes.l  → undefined
theme.space.l      → 1.25rem
fontSize="l"       → emits nothing at all
```

It *is* pre-existing. It's also a **live rendering defect** — the "My Account" popover heading gets no font-size. I treated a style-convention flag as noise because it wasn't in our diff, without checking whether the value resolved. And `zimmTextInput.ts:118` already documents this exact trap for the sibling case (`height: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)'` — *"var, not 'l': theme.sizes has no 'l' key"*), so the pattern was known and written down.

Also important for Stage 2: `recipeGuards.test.ts` walks the recipe map only, so **no extension of it can ever catch this** — it's a JSX prop. That needs a separate ast-grep rule or a direct fix.

## Two more corrections

**S3 — my proposed fix was insufficient.** "Carry the last non-index key forward" fixes only the *array* form; `width: {base:'xl'}` still escapes because `base`/`md` aren't numeric indices. The validator built the working version — detect a responsive *container* (all keys are breakpoint names) — and scored **18/18 with 10 deliberate false-positive controls**, including Chakra's own `sizes: {md, lg}` recipe shape, which must not be misread as responsive. The all-keys check is load-bearing because `xl`/`2xl` exist in *both* `breakpoints` and `spacing`.

**S11 — reframed, and less severe than I said.** The defective half is `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '36px'`, **not** the slot. The slot's rem choice is correct — it tracks the message at constant `0.5625rem` slack across every zoom. Measured divergence:

```
root  slot   field   gap
16px  45     45      0
32px  90     53      37     ← both states still UNDER the slot
```

So the consequence is **over-reservation — 37px of dead space at 200% — not clipping or reflow.** The no-shift guarantee holds. What breaks is the derivation, and therefore the accuracy of the comment I wrote.

And the `sizes` blow-up isn't "20–30×" as I passed along from the manual: measured **8×–112×**, with `s`/`m`/`l` absent entirely so those declarations are silently dropped.

## Stage 1 scoreboard

```
S1  CONFIRMED   3/3 guards pass on empty input
S2  CONFIRMED   3 collapse modes all pass vacuously, proven in a real browser
S3  CONFIRMED   my fix insufficient · working fix supplied, 18/18, 0 false positives
S4  CONFIRMED   10px vs 14px, 4xs emits nothing · + 1 live defect outside guard scope
S11 CONFIRMED   but over-reservation, not reflow · wrong half identified
M1  PARTIAL     comment false ✓, widening real ✓, XOR erasure ✗
M2  CONFIRMED   with two of my terminology/severity errors corrected
S6  CONFIRMED   readonly breaks nothing — verified on a full isolated copy
S7  CONFIRMED   purely type-level, same declarations via `export *`
```

## One incidental finding worth chasing separately

Typing into the subscribe field at 25ms/key **drops leading characters** — `test@example.com` arrived as `example.com`, and submit then correctly rejected it as invalid. Focus, wait ~400ms for the label-float transition, then fill works reliably. That would make any future Playwright or `play` coverage of that field flaky, and it might be a real UX bug in the controlled-input path. Not investigated.

Validator 3 (styling and coverage — S5, S8, S9, S10) is still running. Once it lands I'll launch Stage 2 with the corrected fixes rather than the originally-claimed ones.

text:
Group A done, five items, all proven. Two things stand out.

## The design call got vindicated mid-flight

I told it to use a `> 0` floor rather than pin the exact counts. During its own run a sibling agent registered `ZimmLogo` and the measurement moved **441 entries / 6 recipes → 453 / 7**. A pinned 441 would already be red.

## S3 wasn't as latent as we thought

It found a real 3-element responsive array in the **shipped** theme — `Header.logoBar.paddingTop` at `header.ts:56,59` — that every prop-keyed guard was structurally blind to. Six of 441 leaves reattributed, all there. So the guard gap had live data behind it, not just synthetic cases.

It also improved on my spec twice, both correctly: `BREAKPOINT_KEYS` is **derived** from `foundation/gridSystem`'s breakpoints rather than retyped as a literal — matching the repo's "alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" rule so it can't drift. And it added a `where()` formatter because the `Bad.g.fontSize.fontSize` path-doubling I'd flagged affects *all* the guards' messages, not just the new one.

**And it excluded `fontWeight` on its own judgement**, with the reason recorded: `medium` is a key in both the Zimmermann and Chakra scales and resolves to 500 either way, so the union rule would have flagged a correct declaration. I hadn't thought of that.

## S8 — kept a declaration I'd offered to drop

It retained `fontStyle: 'normal'` because `textStyles.serif` is italic, so keeping it makes the substitution output-identical under *any* ancestor rather than just today's. Proved byte-identical across all 9 properties in both `inverse` modes by expanding through `css()(toCSSVar(theme))` and dereferencing every `--zimm-*` var. `input` part verified untouched by diff.

## S11 — derivation restored

```
              slot   field   gap
root 16px      45     45      0
root 32px      90     89      1     ← was 53 / 37
```

The 1px residue is the deliberately-px border.

## The incidental finding is the most valuable thing here

**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`.** So any test that imports the theme and calls `css(…)(theme)` silently gets every token passed through unresolved. It hit this building the S8 proof: `color: 'text.default'` stayed literal, and even Chakra's own `space.4` failed.

That's the **S1 vacuity pattern one layer down** — an assertion that looks like it's checking resolved CSS and isn't. `theme/index.test.tsx` renders through a provider so it's unaffected, but any future direct-`css()` assertion needs the `toCSSVar` wrap or it passes for the wrong reason.

## State

```
tsc clean · vitest 187/187 (was 185, +2 from recipeGuards) · prettier + eslint clean
nothing staged, nothing committed
```

One honest caveat it raised: `zimmTextInput.test.ts` doesn't assert on the error part's font block or `content.minHeight`, so its green is a no-regression signal for the resolvers rather than direct coverage of these two edits — the offline expansions are the evidence. It flagged two assertions as the natural follow-up and correctly declined to add them to a file outside its remit.

Groups B and C still running.

text:
Group C done — six items, and the mutation matrix is the standout.

## Orthogonal mutation testing

```
mutation                        perm. Tab   perm. scroll   story play
Tab branch early-return          ✗ ✗          ✓             ✗ focus landed on <body>
overflow='hidden' write removed  ✓ ✓          ✗             ✗ expected '' to be 'hidden'
disabled filter removed          ✗ ✗          ✓             n/a
```

Each new assertion is killed by exactly the mutation it targets and no other. That's the standard I wanted and rarely get.

It also **applied the S2 lesson to its own work** — the new scroll-lock assertion captures `overflowBefore` and asserts `not.toBe('hidden')` first, so it can't pass vacuously the way S1 and S2 did.

## Two places it improved on my spec

**The disabled-filter test puts the disabled control at *both* ends** of the focus order. Unfiltered, `first` would be "Disabled leading" and `last` "Disabled trailing" — so neither wrap fires. Stronger than a single control.

**A third test covers the scroll lock restoring a non-empty prior value** (`'scroll'`). That's the half of lines 63-70 a story can never reach, because a story only ever sees `''` restored. I'd have missed it.

## S10 — and it proved its own measurement meant something

```
CONTACT_INDENT → 'l'   heading + 3 link <li> moved 4px → 20px
                       icon-row <li> stayed 0px        ← third case genuinely separate
hug width dropped      Acknowledgement 115px → 160px   ← exactly Stage 1's number
reverted               identical again

You're right to stop and ask. Let me give you my honest read first, then the plan.

## My read, before any agent runs

Of the **13 items** we just put through a four-stage pipeline, I count how many change what a shopper sees: **zero**.

```
M1  inert casts + a false comment        no behaviour change (proven inert)
M2  diagnostic quality in a story        no behaviour change
S1  test guard precondition              test-only
S2  test guard precondition              test-only
S3  guard walker                         1 live instance, in a file we don't own
S4  typography guard                     0 instances in guard scope
S6  readonly                             type-level only
S7  one-word import                      type-level only
S8  textStyle body2                      proven byte-identical
S9  logo → recipe                        0 of 26 baselines moved
S10 style composition                    all baselines identical
S11 rem vs px                            "over-reservation, not clipping"
S5  Tab trap coverage                    tests for a modal that ships disabled
```

S5 is the sharpest example: we built mutation-tested coverage for a focus trap inside a modal we deliberately descoped an hour earlier because it has no design.

Meanwhile the story's AC has real gaps sitting open — the locale label reads `Australia (AUD) / ENG` on all eight storefronts, live AU phone and WhatsApp numbers ship to US/UK/EU/HK/ME shoppers, and there's zero `react-intl` in a component replacing one with 14 translated strings, on a rollout that includes fr/it/es.

And the branch itself is **55 commits, +4541/−105** for a story that says *"footer shell, layout, and component structure only"* and *"without any content behind the different links and buttons."*

Some of the audit has also gone self-referential — `recipeGuards.test.ts` is test infrastructure, and today we spent a full agent pipeline extending it. That's testing the tests.

I'm not going to conclude from that alone that the work is wasted, because there's a real counter-argument I shouldn't dismiss. So let me have that argued properly rather than trust my own first pass.

## The plan

```
WAVE 1 — four agents, parallel, independent

A  Scope ledger      map all 47 files / 4541 lines to: required-by-AC ·
                     required-to-make-an-AC-work · deferred-by-the-story ·
                     not-mentioned-anywhere. Quantified, file by file.

B  Cost of carry     for everything deferred or unmentioned: bundle weight,
                     maintenance surface, sync burden, what must be reworked
                     when the real story lands, what is actively harmful.

C  Opportunity cost  what the AC requires that is missing or wrong, ranked by
                     shopper impact. The counterweight to A and B.

D  The loop itself    audit the audit: of every fix this session, how many moved
                     shopper-visible behaviour? Was the pipeline proportionate?
                     Where did marginal value go to zero?

WAVE 2 — one agent, adversarial

E  Steelman          takes A–D and argues the OPPOSITE. Is what looks like
                     overengineering actually load-bearing? Which atoms are
                     genuinely reused, which rules mandated the recipe, which
                     guard caught something real? Then reconciles.
```

Wave 2 is the recursive part — I don't want my own read standing unchallenged, and I especially don't want an agent agreeing with me because I framed the question.

Then I synthesise into three lists: **keep**, **strip before merge**, **fix before merge** — with the AC as the arbiter, not code quality.

One thing I'd flag about the framing: "overengineering" and "outside scope" are different problems. The modal is outside scope. The recipe guards are arguably in-scope engineering that's disproportionate. They need different answers, so I've asked A and B to keep them separate.

Want me to launch Wave 1?

Wave 1 launched — four agents, independent.

```
A  Scope ledger      every file → REQUIRED / SUPPORTING / DEFERRED / UNMENTIONED,
                     quantified as % of +4541, with the three biggest files
                     broken down internally
B  Cost of carry     measured bundle weight, recurring cost, rework verdict,
                     and a ranked "actively harmful" list
C  Opportunity cost  the AC gaps, confirmed in code or by measurement,
                     ranked P1–P4 by shopper/rollout impact
D  The loop itself    fix ledger classified B/C/T/Y/X with ratios, the
                     self-referential question, proportionality, and the
                     common cause behind the bad checks
```

## How I framed them, and why it matters

**A** has to justify every `SUPPORTING` call by naming what breaks without it. That's the category where "we needed it" quietly absorbs anything, so it's the one I constrained hardest.

**B** must *measure* rather than estimate, and has to separate cost already paid from cost that recurs. It's also told explicitly not to inflate — a one-word import fix costs nothing and should be recorded as costing nothing.

**C** is the counterweight, and it's told plainly: *"I want the real list, not a long one."* If an AC is genuinely met it should say so.

**D** is the one I was most careful with. I told it I'm the one who ran the loop and I'm asking whether it was worth it — and that a defensive answer and a performatively harsh one are equally useless. I also gave it the specific counter-evidence, because the loop *did* catch real errors: a fix that would have regressed the input's line-height, a fix that turned out not to need the API change I'd proposed, and several claims of mine that were overstated or plain wrong. It has to weigh those against the effort, not just tally the effort.

I've asked D one question I don't have a good answer to myself: the **common cause** behind the checks that produced confident nonsense. A static regex reporting four false missing theme parts, three separate times. A case-sensitive grep that broke CI. A parity check that reported everything missing because `baseStyle` is a function. `test-storybook` aimed at a dev server. Two processes writing to one file. Those all have the same shape, and "be more careful" isn't a fix — I explicitly told it that isn't an acceptable answer.

Wave 2 follows: a single adversarial agent that takes A–D and argues the **opposite** case, then reconciles. I don't want my own read standing unchallenged, and I especially don't want four agents agreeing with a conclusion I handed them in the framing.

Nothing is committed. The 13 fixes are still sitting uncommitted in the tree, which is the right place for them until this question is answered — because the answer might be to drop some of them.

The strongest arguments against Wave 1, because these are the ones that could actually overturn its conclusion:

- **The atoms** — `components.md` mandates all variants upfront *because* the Contentful sync is additive-only and a wrong variant model is semi-permanent. If that's right, building the full surface now is the *cheaper* path, and "zero live render sites" is the wrong metric.

I also barred one specific move: **"it's good practice" is not an acceptable justification.** Every KEEP has to tie to an AC, a rule it can cite by file, or a measured cost saving.

text:
Width`, `helperText`, and `size='large'` — which is the *default*.

**Test time is not a cost.** I passed along "48% of suite runtime." Arithmetically right, practically meaningless: the whole suite is **2.19s**, tests run in parallel, and one pre-existing `theme/index.test.tsx` case costs 205ms on its own — more than the modal test.

## The bypass is wider than I reported

```
"/\\example.com"    → https://example.com/
"/\t/evil.com"      → https://evil.com/     ← TAB also passes
"/\n/evil.com"      → https://evil.com/
```

The WHATWG URL parser strips C0 control characters *before* parsing. So the fix isn't "add `\\` to the lookahead" — it's reject backslash **and** strip-or-reject C0/whitespace first. My 13 test cases would have missed all three.

## And one thing that's worse than I said

`overrides/app/components/button/index.tsx` has **zero consumers**. So it isn't "a second Button" — the *older* one is already dead, and nothing in the repo would have flagged it. `AGENTS.md` contains zero occurrences of "registry," and `components.md` has no check-before-you-create rule.

## The strip list — and it's smaller than you'd expect

```
CLEAN LIFTS (~0 cost now)
  contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts   97    zero importers
  primaryInverse + secondaryInverse  78   zero consumers anywhere
  generateRegistry.mjs + AI docs    293   ← also removes frozenFiles.md from the
                                          diff, which is what makes this PR span
                                          Tier 1 + Tier 2 + untiered at once

SEPARABLE (~1 hour)
  the modal                         371   enableNameCapture is already the gate

TOO ENTANGLED — leave, note in the PR
  33 unused ZimmIcon types · clearable · fonts (the blocker is the licence)
```

The modal argument isn't about weight. It's that `Chakra 2.7.0` exports `Modal`, `react-focus-lock` and `react-remove-scroll` are **already installed**, base SFCC uses Chakra `<Modal>` in **28 files** — and `useSubscribeModal` reimplements that infrastructure *less correctly*: no `inert` on background content, the trap only fires when focus is already on first/last, no scrollbar-width compensation. Shipping it sets a precedent the next modal copies.

## The single highest-value action — and it isn't mine

I said the `safeHref` fix. **Wave 2's answer is better: resolve the Futura Round web licence.**

Its reasoning holds: it's the only item with exposure *outside* the codebase; it's the only one where the repo's own Tier 1 documentation **actively misstates what the code does**, so nobody reading the rules will ever look for it; and it's the only one needing someone outside the squad, so it has the longest lead time. One message now, a launch blocker later.

It beats the checkout footer *precisely because* the checkout footer will be caught — `"This is a demo store only. Orders made WILL NOT be processed."` on the payment page is glaring and QA finds it in the first pass. An unlicensed font on the CDN won't be found, because the rules say it isn't happening.

And `safeHref` is latent until HPC-034 connects Contentful, so it can ride with that story.

## What this actually says about the loop

Agent D's headline survived the adversarial pass: **every item on the missed list lives outside the working tree.** A font licence, 18 review threads, a memory doc, a site-config table, a checkout page.

The loop was rigorous about what it could see. On the day it ran hardest it spent its effort on type erasure and comment placement while a Major CodeRabbit finding six hours old named a live security bypass — one I then shipped a fix for, called *"well covered, 3 layers,"* and left open.

The process change worth making is one line: **read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** The queue was already telling us what was wrong.

Nothing is committed. The 13 fixes are still uncommitted, and after all this I'd keep them — they're cheap, verified, and none of them is what's wrong with this branch.

# 4. The 13 fixes — verdict

You asked for a call, so here it is. **None are wrong, none are harmful, and total measured cost is ~2ms of test time.** But they don't all earn a place in this PR.

## Genuinely applicable — 6

| ID | Why it earns its place |
|---|---|
| **S1** | The only change that raises the **validity** of the existing suite. Four guards assert `expect(offenders).toEqual([])`; an empty input satisfies all four. Proven: stub `components` to `{}` and every one still passes. This is the fix for the failure mode that produced most of this session's bad checks |
| **S2** | Same class. Three collapse modes proven to pass vacuously in a real browser, and every rect is 0 in jsdom |
| **S11** | **The only shopper-perceptible item** — restored a derivation that over-reserved 37px at 200% zoom |
| **M1** | The comment was **factually false** and the pattern was already being cited elsewhere. A wrong explanation is worse than none — it invites the next reader to reintroduce the cast |
| **S6** | `FOOTER_FIXTURE` is a module singleton on the **production** data path, and a mutation probe compiles today. Type-only, zero runtime cost, nothing breaks |
| **S7** | One word. `@storybook/react` is undeclared and works purely on npm hoisting — a pnpm or nested install breaks `tsc` on that file |

## Defensible but wouldn't have been done from the review queue — 4

| ID | Honest position |
|---|---|
| **S5** | Covers genuinely untested branches — the Tab trap and scroll lock, with an orthogonal mutation matrix. But it's coverage for a modal that **ships disabled**, and if you strip the modal this goes with it |
| **S3** | Real gap, and it did reattribute 6 live leaves in `header.ts`. But **0 offenders** either way |
| **S4** | Guards a real bug class with **9 live instances** — all of which are JSX props the guard structurally cannot see. The file says so itself, then didn't write the ast-grep rule that would catch them |
| **M2** | Diagnostic-quality only. It threw before and throws now, just with a named error |

## Overengineering — 3

| ID | Why |
|---|---|
| **S8** | Proven **byte-identical** across 9 properties. Nothing was broken; nothing changed |
| **S9** | **0 of 26 baselines moved.** Moved 5 CSS properties into a recipe. Defensible under `overrideStyling.md` rung 3, but nothing was wrong |
| **S10** | All baselines identical at both viewports. Real DRY win on a verbatim duplication, but it also introduced a latent mutual exclusion (`linkListItemHug` now wins over the contact indent where the old code applied both) |

## The verdict in one line

**6 applicable, 4 defensible, 3 overengineering** — and the split maps almost exactly onto *where the finding came from*. The six applicable ones fix things that were actually broken. The seven others came from reading code we'd just written, looking for things to improve.

The strongest argument for committing all 13 anyway: they're implemented, mutation-tested, regression-verified against a full CI-parity run, and reverting them costs more attention than keeping them. The strongest argument against: this PR is already 10–12 hours to review, and 7 of these add surface without fixing anything.

// button.ts sizes.icon

## What each part actually does

```
                                    @375 idle          @375 error         verdict
baseline                  footer 1237 col 163 gap 40   gap 18   Δ0        ✅
A  remove minHeight       footer 1197 col 123 gap 0    Δ22      SHIFTS    load-bearing
B  remove marginTop:auto  footer 1237 col 163 gap 0    Δ0       no shift  gap collapses
C  restore marginBottom   footer 490→511               Δ21      SHIFTS    load-bearing
```

**All three matter, but for two different reasons.**

`minHeight` (A) and removing the body's fixed `marginBottom` (C) are what stop the **shift**. `marginTop: auto` (B) doesn't affect the shift at all — it's what preserves the **40px gap**. Without it the column is the right height but the body sits flush against the field, which is a visual regression a footer-height check would never catch.

My first mutation run at 1440 showed A and B as "no shift" — because the taller site-map column masks the subscribe column there. That's the identical false negative I hit on the submit-state fix, and I walked into it again. Only mobile, where the columns stack, tells the truth.

## The mechanism, matching Figma

```
Figma    Textfield  44 → 61   top moves 98 → 82   section 142 → 143
ours     slot       45 → 67   gap  moves 40 → 18   column 163 → 163
```

The field's bottom edge is anchored and the gap above absorbs the growth — the same thing the design does, reproduced with an auto margin instead of absolute positioning.

The concern is real in general: tests that share global state can poison each other, so test 3 fails only because test 2 ran first.

So **both paths that finish a flow clear it, and the path that abandons one doesn't.** A shopper types their email, the modal opens, they hit Escape — and their address stays in memory. That's the case where you'd least want to keep it, and it's the only one missed.

It's also inconsistent with reasoning already in the file. Line 229 carries a comment saying the record holds customer PII and there's no request for it to outlive. That argument applies with more force to a cancellation than to a submit.

## #1 grammar — **valid concern, wrong correction**

CodeRabbit says `composed from` → `composed of`. I'd push back on that specific change, and the repo tells you why:

```
zimmTokens.ts:[REDACTED]   "All --zimm-* variables, derived from the other foundation/* files"

The relationship is **derivation** — the `.zimm-*` classes are *generated using* the tokens, not *made up of* them. `composed of` would say the classes consist of tokens, which is the wrong claim. LanguageTool is applying a generic collocation rule without the semantics.

But the phrase *is* awkward, so it's worth changing — just to the word the codebase already uses for this exact relationship:

```diff

+ the `.zimm-*` global classes derived from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2)
```

That's unambiguous, grammatically clean, and consistent with `zimmTokens.ts` and `overrideStyling.md`, which both describe this as derivation. It satisfies the finding without accepting a correction that would make the sentence less accurate.

## The finding is correct, and one half is my own bug reintroduced

CodeRabbit raised one actionable item on `generateRegistry.mjs:495-523` — my fix from `13add6e`. Both of its logic claims check out.

**Bug 1 — partial unions reported as complete.** `.filter(Boolean)` silently drops members it can't resolve, and the bail-out only fires when *all* of them fail. For `A | B` where `B` lives in another file, `members` becomes `[A]`, so `members.length === 1` — and then every one of A's props satisfies "present in every member" and stays **required**. A half-known union is published as a complete, fully-required prop set.

**Bug 2 — requiredness depends on declaration order.** I counted *presence*, not optionality, and kept the first occurrence's text verbatim. Proved it by mutation — reversing the two union members in `zimmButton/index.tsx`:

```
before:  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'
after:   variant: 'icon'          ← same type, now claimed required
```

**Third ask — regression tests.** `scripts/` has no test file at all today. This would be the first, i.e. new harness for an unlinted dev script.

**Recommended: fix the two logic bugs, decline the tests, and pre-commit to a stopping rule.**

- Bug 1: bail to the union expression unless *every* member resolves. One condition change.
- Bug 2: track optionality per member — required only if every member declares it without `?`. A few lines.
- Tests: decline. `.claude/rules/testing.md` scopes tests to failures that are non-obvious or costly; a wrong cell in generated dev documentation is neither, and standing up the first `scripts/` test harness for it is disproportionate.

ates 9 locales; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` has 10. The missing one is `en-CA` — the ZimmermannUSIntl locale — while `seedRegions.mjs` cheerfully creates `region-ZimmermannUSIntl` with `locale: 'en-CA'`. Invisible today only because nothing passes a locale. It bites the moment locale-aware fetching lands.

**Your placeholder-contact problem is gone.** `contentfulFixture.ts` was *renamed* to `index.stories.content.ts` and is now imported by exactly one file — the story. The `tel:+61280808080` / `wa.me` values still exist in the repo but are no longer in the production import graph, so they don't ship. Live values come from `footerConfig` and pass through `isSafeHref` with an inert fallback.

## The copy system, and why it was built twice in one day

That's the most instructive seam in the branch.

**`useUiCopy` is now one line:** `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`. Provider mounted at `_app-config/index.tsx:161`, innermost — which puts it *above* the base template's `IntlProvider`, so it's available app-wide.

**Why v1 didn't hold:** the underlying fetch hook is a hand-rolled `useState`/`useEffect`/`fetch` with no cache, no dedup, no query key. Two components calling it meant **two identical network requests**. So v1's prop-drilling wasn't stylistic — threading ten props through three components was the *mitigation*, and one that only worked while exactly one caller existed. v2 shares a single fetch, which is what makes direct calls from anywhere safe. All ten props deleted.

**The load-bearing design decision:** no Provider → returns a fallback rather than throwing. Both `t` parameters are required, so `t('footer.copyright.label', 'Copyright')` always has an answer. That's why the leaves render in Storybook and Vitest with zero setup — a test was deliberately *un*-mocked because of it.

**Where it will surprise you:**

- **The 100-entry cliff.** No `limit` is passed and Contentful's CDA defaults to 100. At entry 101, keys start silently rendering English fallbacks — no error, green tests (they mock the hook, so they structurally cannot catch it). It'll present as "my CMS change didn't take effect."
- **Missing key, still loading, network down, and no provider are all indistinguishable** — same silent fallback, nothing in the console.
- **It bypasses react-intl rather than complementing it.** No locale, not in SSR (English fallback in the HTML, swaps post-hydration), and no review gate — an editor changes production copy with no PR, versus `translations/` which is Tier 2 and Integration-owned. Different risk profile entirely. Decision rule as the code actually behaves: needs editor control without a deploy → uiCopy; needs to be right in SSR HTML, vary by locale today, or interpolate a variable → react-intl.
- Keys are free-form dot-paths with **no typed union** and no check that a key in code exists in the CMS, or vice versa.

**Governance was followed through, mostly.** `components.md` gained an explicit carve-out letting Context-backed app-wide static-copy hooks be called from presentational leaves, naming `useUiCopy` as the reference. That exception is honest — the hook doesn't fetch, it's `useContext`. `uiCopyProvider/` was added to Tier 2 and CODEOWNERS. But note the carve-out does **not** cover `FooterContainer`'s own fetch sitting under `components/` — that remains acknowledged debt, flagged in its own JSDoc as something that should move to an `_app` override. Easy to conflate on a skim.

One small thing that lands on the file I just touched: `generateRegistry.mjs`'s `TIER2_PATHS` is a hardcoded mirror list that wasn't updated, so the registry reports `UiCopyProvider` as feature-local and will keep reproducing that on regeneration.

'3xs' : '50%'` — which shipped precisely because `floated` was false under single-default resolution. He proved it by reintroducing the bare value and confirming failure.

That's the most valuable thing in the two theme commits and it isn't in the commit subject.

## The new hole the mandate opens

Making `var()` mandatory turns a token name from a checked key into an **arbitrary string**. Nothing validates that a referenced var exists — the compound-shorthand guard actively treats `var()` as opaque (`recipeGuards.test.ts:322` replaces it with the literal `VAR`). So `var(--zimm-scale-mm)` emits an unresolved custom property with no TS error and no test failure. All 50 currently-referenced vars do exist, so this is latent, not live. But neither doc acknowledges the trade.

Also: there is **no `--zimm-font-size-l`**, so `header:302` has no var-based remedy at all. The correct fix there is `textStyle`.

## `audit:tokens` — real, useful, and narrower than it sounds

Two regexes: `#hex` and digits followed by `px|rem|em`. Line-based grep, not AST, self-documented as such. Current run: 44 files, **14 unacknowledged violations, 16 acknowledged**, exit 1.

What it cannot see, all proven against real code rather than assumed:

- **`rgba()` / `hsl()` / named colours** — `collectionHero.tsx:31` has `textShadow="0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)"`; it flags `1px` and `4px`, says nothing about the hardcoded colour
- **`vw` / `vh` / `%` / `ch` / `pt`** — `header.ts:73` `min(597px, 60vw)` flags only the px half
- **Bare Chakra numerics and non-Zimmermann colours** — `mb={4}` and `bg="gray.100"` both pass
- **Neither trap.** Confirmed by running the actual regexes over the actual bytes of `header/index.tsx:302`: zero matches. The audit and the traps are orthogonal concerns that happen to share a doc section.

And one genuine hazard in the allow-list: **the marker regex has no word boundaries.** `/provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i` means a comment saying *"depending on the viewport"* matches `pending` and silences every raw literal in its block. Latent today, live-fire the moment someone writes it.

Related: the escape hatch is prose, self-service, unreviewed. `466e62b`'s own remedy for `zimmButton.css.ts` was **rewording a comment** to add "PROVISIONAL" while `'50px'`/`'41px'`/`'5px'` stayed exactly as they were.

## Two corrections to what I told you earlier

**No CI workflow was touched.** I said "CI 1 file" in my first breakdown — that was `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, a *derived* artifact compiled by `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`. `.github/workflows/` is byte-identical across the range: **0 files.** Nothing new is gated. Same for `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` — both untouched.

**The rules file now contradicts itself, and I verified it directly.** `overrideStyling.md:16` says *"**Never** a bare Chakra/theme token string."* 120 lines later, in a section with **0 hunks touched** in Tim's range, `:137-140` still says:

> reference it **by name** in the theme config (`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2`…)

`marginBottom` is in the guard's `SPACE_PROPS` (line 100) and `'xs'` is in `SPACING_KEYS`. So **a developer following §137 inside a registered recipe fails `npm run test`.** The same section also cites `theme/components/imageGallery.ts` and `swatchGroup.ts` as exemplars — neither file exists.

That's the single highest-value fix in the whole change set: one stale section actively instructing a now-blocked pattern.

When it lands I'll do the cross-cutting pass: reconciling the six domains against each other, since several findings already interlock (the `button.ts` gate-drop, the registry tier drift, and the `useZimmModal` 5-consumer threshold all point at the same hand-maintained-mirror problem).

## What it does

`.storybook/main.js`, +13 lines, one file:

```js
webpackConfig.plugins.push(new webpack.DefinePlugin({ WEBPACK_TARGET: "'web'" }));
```

`pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config.js` branches on that global to choose `ssr-config.client.js` over the Node-only `ssr-config.server.js`, which pulls `cosmiconfig` and its `fs`/`os`/`module` deps. The real app build gets it from pwa-kit-dev's own `DefinePlugin`; Storybook's webpack never set it, so the server branch was being bundled and the browser build failed with `Module not found: fs/os/module`.

**It's fallout from his own work.** The trigger is `config/contentful.ts`'s `getConfig()` reaching Storybook via `footer/index.stories.tsx` — which only started importing it when `5640c25` wired the footer to live Contentful. m. The result is worth the detour:

# `test-storybook`: 4 of 83 fail — and it's a required check nobody has run

`Storybook interaction & a11y tests` is a **required** status check that's been reporting `skipping` on recent commits. Run against Tim's branch with a verified-correct server, it fails.

## Failure 1 of 2 — the modal's dialog role (1 test)

`Forms/ZimmSubscribeModal › Default › play-test` → *"Unable to find an accessible element with the role 'dialog'"*

**Not an a11y defect.** `zimmModal/index.tsx:53-54` sets `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` correctly. The problem is line 50: it renders through `createPortal`, so the dialog lands on `document.body` — **outside `canvasElement`**, which is where the `play` function looks.

This is a genuine rule-vs-architecture conflict, and it's new: `.claude/rules/testing.md` says *"Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly."* Tim's extraction of the portal into a reusable `ZimmModal` atom made that rule unfollowable for any portalled component. One of the two has to give.

## Failure 2 of 2 — contrast (3 tests)

All three variants fail axe: *contrast 2.95 (foreground `#969696`, background `#ffffff`, 12px) — expected 4.5:1.*

I nearly reported this as a WCAG defect. It isn't. Computing it properly:

| context | ratio | |
|---|---|---|
| **Real footer** — `#969696` on `background.05` (`#191919`) | **5.94:1** | ✅ PASS |
| Story, as axe measured it — `#969696` on `#ffffff` | 2.96:1 | ❌ FAIL |

The story *declares* `parameters: { backgrounds: { default: 'dark' } }` at line 8 — the author's intent was right. But that background isn't reaching axe inside the test-runner, so it measures the organism against Storybook's default white. **The product is accessible; the harness is measuring the wrong thing.**

Still a real problem, because it fails a required check and would block the merge on a false signal.

Two things surfaced alongside it:

**Tim did change that colour.** Pre-Tim, subscribe body was `var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)` (white, 17.58:1). Now it's `text.inverseGrey` (`#969696`, 5.94:1). Still comfortably passing, but a deliberate contrast reduction worth knowing about as a design decision rather than discovering later.

**The token is already flagged as unresolved.** `foundation/colour.ts:63` carries: *"Handover contradicts itself here: tokens/colors.css says #969696 'confirmed', but tokens.md and contract/zimm-contract.js say #939393 and still flag it unresolved."* Worth noting for whenever that gets settled: **both candidates behave identically here** — `#969696` = 2.96:1 and `#939393` = 3.07:1 on white, both fail; both pass on `#191919`. So the Handover contradiction doesn't affect this outcome either way, and resolving it won't fix the story.

## Correcting myself twice

I got the instrument wrong twice before getting a usable result. First run bound to another session's server on port 6006 while `wait-on` reported success — invalid. Second run aborted on my own bad probe: I grepped the build *log* with `head -1` and picked up a superseded intermediate bundle hash instead of the real entry. Only the third attempt, comparing md5 of served vs on-disk `iframe.html`, was trustworthy. Same failure mode as earlier in this session — the check was built from an assumption rather than from the artifact.

## Verified state

| | |
|---|---|
| `build-storybook` | ✅ clean — `7b9b5dc`'s `WEBPACK_TARGET` fix is real, all stories compile |
| `test-storybook` | ❌ **2 suites / 4 tests fail** (both fixable in story code; product unaffected) |
| `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| `vitest run` | ✅ 252/252 |
| `npm run lint` | ❌ 19 errors, gated nowhere |
| `audit:tokens` | ❌ 14 violations, gated nowhere |

Both doc critics are still out. This finding will need to go into Part 2 of the guide when they land, since it materially changes the "tests and harness" picture — the suite isn't just ungated in places, it's actively red in a place that *is* gated.

**Part 1 is missing the single highest-blast-radius fact in the branch.** It says `button.ts` is "gone — moved, not emptied" and never says where. You only learn it moved to `zimmButton.css.ts:243`, still exporting the `Button` key that styles *every* Chakra button in the app, down in Part 2 — the half you're told not to circulate.

**§4 rests on an undefined term.** "The traps" is used five times, numbered once in a table forty lines after first use, and the mechanism is never explained. The one quantitative claim — `8×–112×` — appears with no derivation. The reviewer's verdict is that you'd finish that section holding the *rule* (`always var(--zimm-*)`) without the *reason*, so the first time someone challenges it in review you're back to reading `theme/index.ts`. Three sentences fix it, and they're the highest-leverage three sentences in the file.

**A real numeric error, which I can confirm from the source reports:** line 48 says v1 "threaded ten resolved strings" — it was **five strings costing ten props** (5 on `FooterProps`, 1 on `BottomBarProps`, 4 on `ZimmSubscribeSectionProps`). Line 321 has it right; line 48 contradicts it, in the arc paragraph the document itself flags as where the reasoning lives.

**"What I do differently now" is at line 601 of 750** — the most reusable page, placed where you'd never reach it twice. Worse, it's inside Part 1's heading scope, so "share Part 1 only" ships your personal to-do list.

Also: no table of contents across 45 headings; Part 1 uses §1–6 and Part 2's patterns *also* use 1–6, so the three internal cross-references are ambiguous; and the `overrideStyling.md` self-contradiction — which the document itself ranks as the #1 highest-value item — is filed under a heading called "Also worth knowing."

About 120 lines are recoverable, mostly repetition: the `audit:tokens`-not-gated fact appears **six times**. Most of that collapses automatically once the Part 1 / Part 2 boundary is fixed.

The reviewer's overall read is that the four things genuinely requiring reasoning are all explained causally and would survive a month — why moving a recipe file is a runtime no-op, why `useUiCopy` had to be rebuilt in a day, why Storybook suddenly needed `WEBPACK_TARGET`, and why CODEOWNERS routing flipped. So the spine is sound; the problems are boundary, definition, and ordering.

Waiting on the fact-checker, then I'll revise against both plus the `test-storybook` finding, and re-verify anything it disputes rather than taking it on faith.

Good push — you were right to interrogate it. **`getProps` offers nothing here, because it isn't enabled in this app.** My original ask was wrong.

## What I found

`route-component/index.js:67` gates the whole mechanism:

```js
const getPropsEnabled = hocs.indexOf(withLegacyGetProps) >= 0;
```

and `shouldGetProps` returns `false` immediately when that's off. This app wraps `_app-config` in **`withReactQuery` only** (`_app-config/index.tsx:245`), same as the base template. So `getProps` is dead code here — no component's `getProps` would ever be called. The only `getProps` calls in `overrides/` are `ContentfulLivePreview.getProps`, an unrelated Live Preview API. My "the codebase references it for exactly this" rested on a single comment in `pages/experience/index.tsx:54`, which is itself aspirational.

## The actual mechanism — and it makes the challenge stronger

`withReactQuery` does the SSR data work:

- `react-ssr-prepass` walks the tree during SSR and resolves React Query suspensions
- `dehydrate(queryClient)` serialises results into `__PRELOADED_STATE__`
- `<Hydrate>` rehydrates on the client with data already present

**And the precedent is right next door:** base `_app/index.jsx:202` loads translations via `useQuery`. That's exactly why translated text appears in the SSR HTML and the footer's copy doesn't.

So the real ask isn't "move to `getProps`" — it's much smaller and much harder to argue with:

> **Why is this a hand-rolled `useState`/`useEffect`/`fetch` when the app's SSR data mechanism is React Query, and the component directly above it in the tree already uses `useQuery` for exactly this shape of problem?**

Swapping to `useQuery` would, in one change:

1. **Put the footer in the SSR HTML** — prepass resolves it, dehydrate serialises it
2. **Remove the client round-trip** on first load
3. **Remove the post-hydration layout shift**
4. **Give it caching and dedup for free** — which independently dissolves the double-fetch problem that forced the entire `useUiCopy` v1→v2 Context refactor

That last one is the interesting part: the whole justification for v1's ten-prop drill was *"no cache, so two callers means two requests."* React Query removes the premise.

## The honest counter-argument

There's a real cost, and Tim may have this reasoning:

`react-ssr-prepass` resolving a Contentful call adds latency to **TTFB on every page**. And the footer is **below the fold** — it isn't the LCP element. So you'd be blocking time-to-first-byte for content that doesn't affect LCP, on a project where mobile page speed is the top priority. Client-side loading for below-fold content is a defensible choice, not obviously wrong.

Two things weaken that defence though: MRT caches SSR responses, so the cost is per-cache-miss rather than per-request; and `uiCopy` is *already* firing an uncached app-wide CDA call on every route client-side, so the round-trips are happening anyway — consolidating them into cached React Query queries is likely net faster, not slower.

## Where I'd now pitch it

Drop the SEO framing to a secondary point — I overstated it. Google does execute JS; "invisible to crawlers" isn't right. The two solid arguments are:

- **CLS.** A full-height footer inserting post-hydration with no reserved space is a Core Web Vital regression, measurable, on a project with an explicit performance budget.
- **Total absence on JS failure**, including Privacy Policy, Terms, Accessibility and Modern Slavery.

**The ask, revised:** *"The app uses React Query for SSR data and `getProps` is disabled — why a hand-rolled fetch here? If it's a deliberate below-the-fold/TTFB trade, let's record it, because it also costs us the cache that `useUiCopy` had to be refactored around."*

That's a question about a mechanism choice with a concrete alternative, which is much more likely to land than a process complaint.

Want to move to item 2, or pressure-test this one further first?

text:
Precise question. Let me verify the one thing I'd be asserting about it.

Confirmed both things I needed. Here's the precise answer.

## Not having `getProps` means React Query is the *only* door to SSR data

In this app, data reaches server-rendered HTML by exactly one route: a React Query query resolved during `react-ssr-prepass`, dehydrated into `__PRELOADED_STATE__`, rehydrated on the client. There is no second path.

So the consequence for the footer is sharper than "a trade-off was made":

**A hand-rolled `useState`/`useEffect`/`fetch` in this app is structurally, unavoidably client-only.** Not deprioritised — impossible. There is no server-side escape hatch for data fetched outside React Query. The moment that mechanism was chosen, SSR was off the table as a matter of plumbing, not judgement.

That reframes the challenge usefully. It's no longer "which of two SSR strategies did you weigh" — there was nothing to weigh. It's: *the footer's data doesn't go through the one mechanism that can server-render it.* Either it uses `useQuery` and appears in the HTML, or it doesn't and can't. No architectural debate left in the middle.

## It also means my original ask was incoherent

"Move it to `getProps`" would have required first enabling `withLegacyGetProps` on `_app-config` — a Tier 1 change to the rendering pipeline — in order to adopt the mechanism Salesforce explicitly named *legacy* and superseded with the one already installed. That's a bigger and worse change than the actual fix. Good thing you asked.

## The one thing the absence genuinely costs — and it isn't the footer's problem

`getProps` receives Express `req` and `res`:

> *"Note that `req` and `res` are only defined on the server – the only place the code actually has access to Express requests or responses."*

That makes it the only place a component can set an **HTTP status code or cache header at SSR time**. Which is precisely why `pages/experience/index.tsx:54` says *"A real 404 needs SSR prefetch (getProps)"* — React Query's prepass can render 404 *content* but cannot send a 404 *status*. Real gap, separate ticket, nothing to do with the footer.

## What it doesn't mean

Not having `getProps` isn't a misconfiguration, doesn't prevent SSR, and isn't the cause of the footer being client-only. `withReactQuery` is the correct modern setup and does the job. The footer is client-only because it opted out of it.

---

**So the challenge on item 1 reduces to one sentence:** *the footer fetches outside React Query, which is the only mechanism in this app that can server-render data — was that deliberate, and if so what's the reasoning, given it also forfeits the cache that `useUiCopy` had to be restructured to work around?*

Ready for item 2 when you are.

text:
pp`, `_app-config`, `_document`, `_error`, and the routed pages. The footer is rendered *inside* `_app`'s layout, so it's not in that chain.

So the footer's fetch would move to an **`_app` override** — which doesn't exist today, and creating one is Tier 2 Global Shell ("Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching").

## What it would look like

```tsx
// overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx  ← new file, Tier 2
ZimmApp.getProps = async ({site, locale}) => {
  const client = createClient({space, environment, accessToken, host});
  const {items} = await client.getEntries({
    content_type: 'footerConfig',
    include: 3,
    locale,                                  // ← free win: locale is available here
  });
  const resolved = pickMostSpecificByRegion(items, site.id);
  return {footerData: resolved ? scopeToRegion(resolved, site.id) : null};
};
```

Note `site` and `locale` arrive as arguments — `AppConfig.extraGetPropsArgs` already injects `buildUrl`, `site` and `locale` into every `getProps` call. No hooks needed, which is the point: `getProps` runs outside React, so `useMultiSite()` isn't available to it. That plumbing exists today and is unused.

## How it would work per request

1. Request hits MRT → Express
2. SDK calls `shouldGetProps` → true (if `withLegacyGetProps` is enabled)
3. `ZimmApp.getProps({req, res, params, location, site, locale})` runs **on the server**, awaiting the Contentful call
4. Result merged into App's props
5. `renderToString` runs with `footerData` already present → **the footer is in the HTML**
6. Props serialised into `__PRELOADED_STATE__`
7. Client hydrates with the same props — no refetch, no layout shift
8. On client-side route changes, `shouldGetProps` decides whether to re-run it

## What changes in the footer itself

`FooterContainer` **disappears entirely**. No `useState`, no `useEffect`, no `if (!footerData) return null`. `Footer` becomes what it already almost is — a pure presentational component receiving `data` as a prop, this time from `_app` rather than from a sibling container.

That's genuinely tidier, and it resolves the container/presentational violation Tim's own JSDoc flags: *"this puts a fetch inside `components/`, which components.md reserves for containers… this should move into an `_app` override instead."* He named this exact solution.

## The wrinkle that kills it

**Base `_app` renders `<Footer />` with no props.** So to get `footerData` into it you'd have to either:

- **reimplement `_app`'s whole layout** in the override so you control the `<Footer data={...} />` call site — a large Tier 2 surface that then drifts from the base template on every upstream bump, or
- **put `footerData` into a Context** in the override and have `Footer` read it — at which point you've built a second `UiCopyProvider`, just fed from `getProps` instead of a hook

So the `getProps` path costs you: enabling a **legacy** HOC (`withLegacyGetProps`, Tier 1 pipeline change), creating an **`_app` override** (Tier 2), *and* a Context or a layout reimplementation anyway — and you still get **no caching, no dedup, no stale-while-revalidate**, because `getProps` is just an imperative async function. You'd hand-roll all of that.

## Versus `useQuery`

```tsx
const {data} = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['footerConfig', site.id],
  queryFn: () => client.getEntries({content_type: 'footerConfig', include: 3}),
});
```

Same SSR outcome — `react-ssr-prepass` resolves it, `dehydrate` serialises it, footer lands in the HTML. Plus caching and dedup for free. `FooterContainer` stays where it is, keeps using `useMultiSite()`, no Tier 1 or Tier 2 change, roughly a five-line diff.

**So: `getProps` would work, and it would produce a cleaner component hierarchy — but it's the expensive route to an outcome `useQuery` gives you for almost nothing.** Worth knowing it exists mainly because it explains why `pages/experience/index.tsx` wants it for a real 404 status, which React Query genuinely cannot do.

Item 2 next?

Its escape hatch ("provide a story-local portal target") does work — but only by **adding a portal-container prop to a shared atom purely to satisfy a test-style rule.** That's production API surface bought with no product value.

## Why these keep coming back — and the real fix

This is the third time this objection has been raised on this PR. The cause is on our side:

`testing.md:128` says, unconditionally, *"Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly."* There is **no portal exception written anywhere.** Meanwhile `footer/index.stories.tsx:123` cites *"testing.md §Layer-2 exception"* — **a section that does not exist.**

So our own rule says the code is wrong, and the only record of the carve-out is inline comments. CodeRabbit is reading the rule correctly and we're the ones out of step. Until that exception is written down, it will re-raise on every push. `.claude/rules/` is Tier 1, so that's an ~8-line amendment behind the governance gate — and it's the durable fix, not another reply.

## Quick wins — #7 and #8

**#7:** CodeRabbit said "extract the content type ID to a named constant." Correct instinct, but it missed that **`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` already exists** at `contentfulMapping.ts:53` — with a `ContentTypeId` type and **zero consumers**. I verified both. Its suggestion would have created a *second* source of truth for the same string. Two lines to import the existing one instead.

**#8:** graded Major, actually cosmetic — the file's only mock is created inside one test body, so `clearAllMocks` provably clears nothing. Running both variants gave identical 4/4 results. **But comply anyway**: I set the precedent on this very PR in `a207b9a` by complying with the identical finding on `zimmTextInput.test.ts`. Declining here after complying there is an inconsistency a reviewer would rightly call out. Five lines.

## Declines worth knowing about

**#9 cites a rule that doesn't exist here.** `conventions.md` says Zimmermann-authored files use **camelCase**; only files mirroring a base Salesforce file keep kebab-case. There is no base SFCC font-face module — zero hits in the package. And the rename would break `.storybook/preview.tsx`'s import, forcing a **Tier 1 edit to satisfy a non-existent rule.**

## Two more false claims — same pattern as the HPC-025 one

**"At 2, every link silently drops out of its scoped column"** — wrong, and the truth is worse. The agent ran the actual `contentful-resolve-response` resolver on a real-shaped payload:

```
regions[0].fields  = undefined
filterByRegion THREW: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'siteId')
```

`isEligible` reads `region.fields.siteId`, so it **throws**. The bare `.catch` swallows it, `footerData` stays null, and the **entire footer renders nothing** — columns, logo band, bottom bar, all of it. Not links quietly dropping. Comment rewritten to say that.

**"`useContentful.ts` uses 2 for flat content types that have no link fields"** — wrong. Its own adjacent comments say it's for **asset** resolution, and the same hook is called with `'homepage'`, whose type has three link fields. Corrected.

## Three defects in my own #9 work

**The JSDoc said "non-global"** — but the warn fires on global ties too, since `Infinity === Infinity` reaches the tie branch. Measured firing once. Fixed.

**The runtime message still promised "most-recently-updated"** when `sys.id` may decide it. I updated the JSDoc and forgot the string. Fixed.

**And my test named "warns on a tie regardless of which side wins" didn't test that.** It passed `[beta, alpha]` — the order where the candidate wins, so the warn fires even nested inside the comparison. It survived that exact mutation. Renamed and flipped to `[alpha, beta]`.

The agent also found a regression my suite missed entirely: dropping the `===` guard promotes `sys.id` to primary key, and **both** my fixture pairs happened to sort id-wise in the same direction as their timestamps, so nothing caught it. Added `zeta`(newer)/`alpha`(older) — deliberately opposed — plus an unscoped-tie case.

## One correction to me, in my favour

I said the warn fires "on every footer render." It doesn't — the call sits in `useEffect(..., [client, site.id])` with a memoised client, so it's **once per mount**, client-side only. Still ungated by `NODE_ENV`, so it does reach shopper consoles.

**All three Contentful ones can be fixed in code now.** I said they "need Contentful access." That's wrong: the *code* changes are repo-only. What needs access is someone **running** the script afterwards. That's a handoff, not a blocker on the commit.

## Fix now — 3

| | Change | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **`installTemplate.mjs:129`** | Compute the unresolved-findings set properly instead of the `conflictingIds.length && TAKEOVER_IDS.length` heuristic | None — strictly *tightens* the gate. Can't cause a bad install |
| **`bootstrapSpace.mjs`** | Move locale provisioning above environment cloning, and loop over `['master', ...TARGET_ENVIRONMENTS]` | Repo-only. Fixes the hole where `locale.create` is hardcoded to `master` |
| **`seedRegions.mjs` / `en-CA`** | Add `en-CA` to the provisioned list | One line — **but inert without the ordering fix**, so it ships with it |

**Defer the part CodeRabbit actually asked for on `bootstrapSpace`** — the `locale.update` reconciliation loop. That's a write path against a live space, needs the `internal_code: undefined` workaround, and `default` reassignment has ordering constraints Contentful enforces. One caveat worth stating in the reply: fixing the code repairs nothing until someone runs it, and adding `en-CA` to a space is a real CMS mutation — additive and non-destructive, but it should go through whoever owns that space.

## Reply only — 2

**`uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:19`** — accept and widen it. CodeRabbit flagged one call site; there are **four across three fetch paths**, and the one it *didn't* flag is worse — `footer/index.tsx`'s `include: 3` pulls nested `footerNavGroup` and `link` entries, so more localized fields ride on it. Adding `locale?` to `useContentfulEntries` is a shared-hook signature change, which `AGENTS.md`'s stop-table sends to a team RFC. Reply + ticket covering locale threading, the `'en-US'`-vs-`'en'` fallback inconsistency, and a non-default-locale test.

**`experience/index.tsx:41`** — agree, defer with a ticket. **`zimmModal.css.ts:30`.** Real WCAG 1.4.10 failure — panel has no `maxHeight`/`overflow`, overlay is `fixed` with `align-items:center` and body scroll locked, so tall content clips *above* the viewport with no scroll path. Two lines:

```ts
maxHeight: '100%',
overflowY: 'auto',
```

`maxHeight: '100%'` rather than the `calc(100dvh − …)` CodeRabbit proposed — that restates the overlay's padding in a second place.

Making the changes first, then adversarial verification. Reading both files.

Now the changes. Starting with `bootstrapSpace.mjs` — `en-CA`, plus extracting locale provisioning so it can run per-environment.

Now replacing the old master-only locales block with a per-environment backfill.

Two sections numbered 4 — renumbering the rest.

Now the third change — the validation gate in `installTemplate.mjs`.

All three applied. Now the closed-loop verification — two adversarial agents, since I can't run these scripts against the live space.

Both files were already prettier-non-conformant at HEAD and still are — so no regression, and reformatting would churn files outside `npm run lint`'s scope. Now the closed loop.

Three changes applied, closed loop running.

## What I changed

**`bootstrapSpace.mjs`** — `en-CA` added, locale provisioning extracted into `provisionLocales(client, environmentId)`, and `main()` reordered: locales into `master` **first**, then environments clone (inheriting them), then a back-fill pass across a new `provisionable` array for environments that already existed.

That last part is the actual fix. The bug was structural — `locale.create` hardcoded to `'master'`, running *after* cloning. A clone inherits master's locales only as they stood at clone time, so any environment created before a locale was added never gets it, and nothing back-fills. Adding `en-CA` alone would have reached `master` and nowhere else.

**`installTemplate.mjs`** — the gate now computes an explicit `unresolved` set instead of `!(conflictingIds.length && TAKEOVER_IDS.length)`. The old expression asked *"is there at least one conflict and at least one takeover?"* rather than *"is every finding accounted for"*, so a single `--takeover` opened the gate for every other finding, including conflicts it never named. Also added a warning when `--takeover` names an id that isn't in the conflict list.

## Verified so far

`node --check` both · `tsc` exit 0 · vitest **257/257** · prettier status **unchanged from HEAD** (both files were already non-conformant, and `scripts/` sits outside `npm run lint`'s `overrides/**` scope, so reformatting would be churn).

## Two agents on it

**Simulation** — extracting the functions into a harness with a stub client that records calls instead of making them, driving six scenarios: empty space, re-run with all environments present, failed/orphaned environment, `--dry-run`, idempotency, and whether the new `"<env>/<code>"` bookkeeping shape breaks any downstream consumer. Plus a full truth table on the gate.

**Safety** — attacking it. Whether the reorder creates a destructive path that didn't exist (locale creation now runs against five more environments), whether the back-fill can hit a non-existent environment, and the one that matters most: **is the new gate ever looser than the old one in any input combination.** If it is, that's a regression, not an improvement.

Both are under a hard prohibition on executing anything in `scripts/contentful/` — including `--dry-run`, which still constructs a client and issues reads against the live space.

I'll report when they land, fix anything found, and only then propose the commit and the three replies.

## What the safety review caught — three were bugs I introduced

**`--dry-run` would have crashed on a fresh space.** My `provisionable` array was populated inside the `DRY_RUN` branch — for an environment the script had *just established doesn't exist*. The back-fill then reads its locales, 404s outside the try/catch, and exits 1 before API keys and the production alias are even previewed. I broke dry-run in exactly the scenario it exists for. Fixed by not pushing there — a clone inherits master's locales anyway, so it needs no back-fill.

**`default: true` would have been POSTed to five more live environments.** The SDK strips `default` on *update* but sends it verbatim on *create*. So if any environment lacked `en` and had a different default, we'd have posted a second default locale — either rejected, or **accepted and silently demoting the incumbent**, which changes what the CDA returns for unlocalized reads. The reviewer couldn't determine which without calling the API, and correctly refused to. `default` is now only ever asserted on `master`.

**And I wrote a warning that lied.** My new `--takeover` message said *"Adopting nothing for them"* while the code still built the takeover payload from **all** ids including unknowns — so a typo'd id was still sent to Contentful as a content type to adopt. That's the same pattern as the HPC-025 citation and the "every link drops out" comment: asserting a property the code doesn't implement. Now filtered to ids Contentful actually reported as conflicting.

**Plus one I widened rather than created:** locale failures were swallowed with exit 0. That covered one environment before; my change made it six, and failures cascade — if `en` fails, the nine locales declaring `fallbackCode: 'en'` fail too. Ten warnings, exit 0. Now exits non-zero.

**The gate change came back clean** — proven a strict tightening across the full input space, with no combination where the old refused and the new proceeds.

## Also reconciled

`README.md:122` said *"One-time space bootstrap. Never re-run against an already-set-up space"* — which my change directly contradicts, since re-running is now how a new locale reaches existing environments. Rewritten to describe the idempotent behaviour and the non-zero exit.

## Three things I'm not doing, flagging instead

**`bootstrapSpace.mjs` has no owner.** It's absent from both `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS`, so it falls to Tier 4 by omission — while `installTemplate.mjs` beside it is Tier 2. That's backwards: `bootstrapSpace` writes locales to production `master`, mints API keys and flips the `production` alias. Adding it needs a Tier 1 governance change.

**`--target` has no production allowlist**, so `install:contentful -- --target master --force --delete-deleted-fields` is reachable in one command, against what `protectedFiles.md` calls the operation that's "difficult to undo". Pre-existing, and the guard pattern already exists in `promoteAlias.mjs`.

**This PR now spans two tiers** — Tier 2 `installTemplate.mjs` and unowned `bootstrapSpace.mjs`. Hard Rule #10 territory, and worth your confirmation before it merges.

text:
# The 4 files, plainly

## 1. `bootstrapSpace.mjs` — the script that sets up Contentful

**What it does:** creates the six Contentful environments (dev, test, sit, staging, uat, master), adds the languages, mints API keys, and points the `production` alias.

**The bug:** it added languages to `master` *after* copying `master` into the five other environments. Copies are snapshots — whatever you add to the original afterwards never reaches them. So a language added later existed in exactly one place, and re-running didn't help because the code only ever wrote to `master`.

That's why `en-CA` was missing. Canadian English was added to the project on 7 August but never to this list, and even adding it would only have fixed `master`.

**Three changes:**
- Added `en-CA`
- Languages now go in **before** the copies are made, so new environments inherit them
- A second pass afterwards back-fills environments that already existed

**Then the safety review found I'd broken things:**
- In preview mode (`--dry-run`) it tried to read languages from environments that don't exist yet → crash, before showing you the rest of the plan
- It would have told five live environments *"this is your default language"* — which either errors, or **silently changes what language the site falls back to**
- If every language failed to create, the script still reported success

All three fixed.

## 2. `installTemplate.mjs` — pushes the content model to an environment

**What it does:** before installing, it asks Contentful "any problems?" and refuses if there are.

**The bug, in plain terms:** the check asked *"is there at least one problem I know about, and did you tell me to ignore at least one thing?"* — instead of *"have you accounted for every problem?"*

So if Contentful reported two problems and you said "ignore the first one," it ignored **both** and installed anyway.

**The fix:** it now works out precisely which problems you've accounted for and refuses if any remain. Proven a strict tightening — nothing that used to be blocked now gets through.

Plus two smaller things: preview mode used to say *"would install"* even when the real run would refuse, and a typo'd ignore-instruction was still sent to Contentful as a real instruction.

## 3. `README.md` — one line

It said *"One-time space bootstrap. **Never re-run** against an already-set-up space."*

But re-running is now exactly how a new language reaches existing environments. So the instructions forbade the thing the fix depends on. Rewritten.

## 4. `.docs/memory/projectState.md` — one line

It said the script "provisions 9 locales without `en-CA`." True this morning, false now. Updated — and it still records the part that **isn't** fixed.

---

## The bit that matters most

**None of this fixes `/en-ca/` yet.** The code is right; nobody has run it. Until someone with Contentful access does, Canadian English still doesn't exist in the space, and every Experience page on the US-International storefront still returns a 400 and shows "Page not found."

I haven't run it and won't — these scripts write to the live CMS, including production `master`. That's a deliberate handoff, not an oversight.

Two other things worth knowing: `bootstrapSpace.mjs` is the higher-risk file of the two — it touches production and mints credentials — and it's the one with **no owner in CODEOWNERS**. And there's one question the review couldn't settle without calling the live API: whether Contentful *rejects* a duplicate default language or *accepts and silently switches it*. That's the difference between my fix preventing noise and preventing real damage, and it's worth testing on a throwaway environment first.

Everything's in place. Here's the answer.

## The command

```bash
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui
```

The workflow takes a **branch or tag** — `feature/my-story` is literally in the input description, so deploying an unmerged branch is supported, not a workaround. Test is the fast disposable quick-look tier.

## Prerequisites — all satisfied

| | |
|---|---|
| `MRT_USER` / `MRT_API_KEY` | ✅ present at repo level |
| `test` environment reviewers | ✅ **none** — runs immediately, no approval wait |
| Version downgrade guard | ✅ skips non-`v*` refs, so a branch passes |
| Prior test deployments | **0** — this would be the first, so no baseline to downgrade from |

## What happens after the push

It's **deploy-then-gate**, deliberately — Test deploys first, then verifies:

1. `deploy-test` → `npm run push:test` (`pwa-kit-dev push -t test`)
2. `bundle-size` → `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing `main.js` ≤ 180 kB and `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB
3. `test-gate` → aggregates the signals

That aggregate result is the "safe to promote to SIT" signal.

## Two things worth weighing first

**You'd be putting an unmerged branch on a shared tier.** Test stays on this branch until someone deploys something else over it — and anyone can dispatch this workflow. Same clobbering dynamic we've seen on the shared MRT dev target. Fine for a quick look; worth a heads-up to whoever else might be using Test.

**Bundle size is the one thing that could fail**, and nobody's run it against this branch. The footer work added `ui-kits/`, the Contentful SDK path and `useUiCopy`, so `vendor.js` is the risk. I can check that locally in a couple of minutes with `npm run test:max-file-size` before you dispatch — cheaper than finding out from a red gate.

## If you'd rather do it properly

Cut an RC tag instead of deploying a branch ref — any developer can:

```bash
git checkout feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui && git pull --ff-only
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

That gives you an immutable, traceable artifact rather than a moving branch ref, and it's what the promotion model expects. Note the tag must be annotated — the pre-push hook rejects malformed `v*` tags.

Deploy at 11:21 **succeeded**; your 403 was at 11:35. So the bundle pushed fine — this isn't a build or deploy failure. Let me find what's actually blocking.

Found something important. Let me confirm it.

That's the answer, and it's not your code.

## The bundle uploaded but was never deployed

The push step's complete output is two lines:

```
info: Beginning upload to https://cloud.mobify.com
success: Bundle Uploaded
```

That's it. **"Bundle Uploaded" is not "deployed."** `pwa-kit-dev push -t test` should upload *and* activate the bundle on the `test` target, and an activation would log it. Nothing did.

So the bundle is sitting in the MRT bundle library, unactivated, and `zimmermann-test...exp-delivery.com` has no live bundle to serve. CloudFront has a distribution but no origin to route to — which is exactly what produces `403 / Request blocked` with `x-cache: Error from cloudfront` and no origin headers. The request never reached an app.

## Why the target isn't resolving

**`mobify.config.js` does not exist in this repo.** That's the file declaring MRT targets, and `AGENTS.md` lists it as Tier 1 runtime config. Without it, `-t test` has no target definition to resolve against — so the CLI uploads the bundle and stops.

This is a known gap, already recorded. `.docs/memory/projectState.md:24`:

> Pending: SFCC SIT credentials, `MRT_SIT_URL` / `MRT_TEST_URL` GitHub Secrets, `push:sit` / `activate:sit` npm scripts, **`mobify.config.js` `sit` env entry**, `config/sit.js`

The note is about `sit`, but the file is missing outright, so `test` has the same problem.

## Why the workflow still went green

`push:test` exits 0 after a successful upload, so `deploy-test` passed, `bundle-size` passed, and `test-gate` aggregated two successes. **The pipeline reports "deployed" when it has only uploaded.** That's a real gap in the gate — worth raising separately, because it'll keep happening silently.

Worth noting the earlier "successful" test deploys on 08-11, 08-06 and 07-30 have the same shape, so it's likely none of them activated either.

## To confirm and fix

**Confirm in the MRT console** — Managed Runtime → your project → Test environment. If the bundle list shows today's build present but not deployed, that's it conclusively.

**Fastest unblock:** activate the bundle manually in the MRT console. One click, no code change.

**Proper fix:** add `mobify.config.js` with the target definitions. That's **Tier 1** under `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule #4-adjacent config — Integration/SI Partner owned — so it needs their sign-off, and I'd want the real MRT project slug and target names from the console rather than guessing them.

One thing I can't check from here: whether the MRT project uses a `.mobify` credentials file or environment-level target config instead. If `pwa-kit-dev` is authenticating fine but has no target map, the console will show it immediately.

**Access Control on the TEST environment.** Tim enabled header-based access control at 11:35 AM today — `x-sfdc-access-control`, value masked to `****YW23`. Only requests carrying that header get past the CDN.

The header isn't in GitHub config at all — but that search turned up something you'll want to deal with first.

## Answer to your question

**The header isn't in GitHub config.** Not as a secret, not as a variable, in any environment. And `grep` across workflows, scripts and docs found no reference to `x-sfdc-access-control` either. It exists only in the MRT console, so Tim is currently the only route to the value.

That's also why nothing in CI would survive being pointed at TEST — there's nothing for a workflow to send.

## But the search surfaced something you should deal with first

**Credentials are stored as GitHub *variables*, not secrets, across five environments.** Variables are readable by anyone with repo read access, are returned in plaintext by the API, and are **not masked in workflow logs**.

```
dev      CODERABBIT_API_KEY  CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN  CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN  PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET
test     CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN  CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN  PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET
sit      (same three)
staging  (same three)
uat      (same three)
```

Ranked by how much I'd worry:

**`PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET` — the real problem.** It's the shopper-authentication credential, and it's stored **both** as a proper repo secret *and* as a plaintext variable in all five environments. The secret version proves the team knows it belongs in secrets; the variable copies undermine it entirely. I read all five values back in plaintext with a routine `gh variable list`.

**`CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`** — grants read access to unpublished draft content. `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` is Tier 1 specifically because it "gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production". Storing the token in plaintext works around that gate from the other side.

**`CODERABBIT_API_KEY`** (dev only) — a paid third-party API key.

**`CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN`** — defensible. CDA tokens are read-only and ship to the browser anyway; `config/contentful.ts` treats it as a public identifier.

This also cuts against `AGENTS.md`: *"Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase"*, and `.env.sample`'s `scope:` convention exists precisely to separate shared/public identifiers from genuine secrets. `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` — Tier 2, Integration/SI-owned — is what pushes these, so the scope-parsing logic there is where the classification is decided.

**I have not changed anything.** Moving them to secrets means rotating them too, since they've been readable, and `switchEnv.mjs`'s push logic would need to match — that's Integration/SI territory, not a unilateral fix.
